1:8.headline: Your mother's teaching: a real mother, or the nation's sages?
1:8.body: Ibn Ezra reads it plainly: a wise mother guides her son, as Bathsheba taught King Lemuel. Rashi reads the father as God, who gave Moses the Torah, and the mother as the people of Israel, whose sages built fences around it.

sources.quote: כי האשה חכמה מורה הדרך הישרה לבנה, כבת שבע שהיא יסרה למואל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says a wise woman shows her son the right way, as Bathsheba taught Lemuel.

sources.quote: מַה שֶּׁנָּתַן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה בִּכְתָב וְעַל פֶּה
sources.says: Rashi says your father's discipline is what God gave Moses, written and oral.

sources.quote: אוּמָּתְךָ, כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Rashi says your mother is your nation, the people of Israel.

sources.quote: וְהֵם דִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים, שֶׁחִדְּשׁוּ וְהוֹסִיפוּ וְעָשׂוּ סְיָגִים לַתּוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi says her teaching is the words of the scribes, who added rules and made fences around the Torah.

1:9.headline: Why the neck is plural: the windpipe is a stack of rings
1:9.body: גרגרות is an unusual plural word for the neck. Rashi says it is plural because the windpipe is made of ring after ring. Ibn Ezra says the word names the area around the throat.

sources.quote: וְעַל שֵׁם שֶׁהַקָּנֶה עֲשׂוּיָה טַבָּעוֹת טַבָּעוֹת, קוֹרֵא הַצַּוָּאר בִּלְשׁוֹן רַבִּים
sources.says: Rashi says the neck is called by a plural word because the windpipe is made of rings.

sources.quote: סביבות הגרון נקראו גרגרות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the area around the throat is called גרגרות.

1:10.headline: A word that looks like 'come' but means 'agree'
1:10.body: תבא looks like the word for 'come'. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it from אבה, to be willing: if sinners try to lure you, do not agree to them.

sources.quote: אַל תֹּבֵא. אַל תֹּאבֶה לָהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says it means do not be willing to go along with them.

sources.quote: תבא. ענין רצון כמו לא אבה יבמי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means wanting, as in 'my brother-in-law is not willing' in Deuteronomy 25.

1:11.headline: Ambushing the innocent for no reason, or in vain?
1:11.body: חנם can mean 'without cause' or 'for nothing'. Metzudat David hears it in the robbers' mouths: we will ambush an innocent man who did no wrong. Rashi says it is the verse's own comment on them: their ambush will come to nothing.

sources.quote: נסתר לארוב על דם נקי לשפוך חנם על לא חמס בכפו
sources.says: Metzudat David says they hide to ambush innocent blood, to spill it for no reason, though he did no wrong.

sources.quote: הַכָּתוּב אוֹמֵר שֶׁצְּפִינָתָם לְנָקִי – חִנָּם הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says the verse itself is saying that their lying in wait for the innocent is in vain.

sources.quote: חנם - מלשון: חנן אלהים מלשון מתנה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says חנם comes from the word for a gift.

1:17.headline: To the bird, the grain on the net looks free
1:17.body: חנם can mean 'free' or 'for no reason'. Rashi says the birds see grain scattered on the net and take it as free food. Ralbag reads 'without cause': the bird never wronged the hunter.

sources.quote: כִּי הָעוֹפוֹת הָרוֹאוֹת חִטִּים וְקִטְנִיּוֹת מְזוֹרִים עַל הָרֶשֶׁת, חִנָּם הוּא בְּעֵינֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the birds see wheat and beans scattered on the net, and it looks free to them.

sources.quote: כמו שנדמה בעיני כל בעל כנף שעל חנם פרושה הרשת ואין הכוונה על הלכידה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it seems to every bird that the net is spread for nothing, not to catch it.

sources.quote: ללכוד בה כי העוף לא חטא למי שהוא צד אותה
sources.says: Ralbag says the net is spread to catch the bird for no reason, since the bird did no wrong to the hunter.

1:20.headline: Wisdom calls out in the plural: many wisdoms, one voice
1:20.body: חכמות is plural, 'wisdoms', yet the verse goes on to give it one voice. Ralbag says the plural fits the outdoors, where many things show many kinds of wisdom. Rashi reads it as the Torah's many teachings, crying out in the study halls.

sources.quote: ואמר חכמות בחוץ תרונה בלשון רבות לפי שבחוץ יראו דברים רבים יעידו על חכמות רבות נפלאות
sources.says: Ralbag says the verse uses the plural because outdoors one sees many things that show many wonderful wisdoms.

sources.quote: הֲרֵי חָכְמוֹתֶיהָ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה בְּחוּצוֹתֶיהָ תִּזְעַקְנָה
sources.says: Rashi says the wisdoms of the Torah cry out in its streets.

sources.quote: וּמָה הֵן חוּצוֹתֶיהָ? בָּתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says its streets are the study halls.

1:26.headline: Your disaster, or a dark mist rising over you?
1:26.body: איד usually means disaster. Ibn Ezra suggests it may come from אד, the mist that rose from the earth in Genesis 2: a day of cloud and fog.

sources.quote: ענין צער ומקרה רע כמו הלא איד לעול
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means pain and misfortune, as in Job 31:3.

sources.quote: יתכן שהוא מלשון ואיד יעלה, כענין יום ענן וערפל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it may come from the mist that 'rose up', like a day of cloud and fog.

10:4.headline: The hand of the busy, or of those who decide honestly
10:4.body: חרוץ can mean busy or decided, and Metzudat Zion and Metzudat David read it as hard-working people. Rashi reads it as the upright, who decide a matter truthfully and without wrong.

sources.quote: חרוצים. עניינו תנועה וזרוזות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means movement and quickness.

sources.quote: היד של הזריזים המתנועעים וטורחים על מזונם
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is the hand of the quick, who move about and work for their food.

sources.quote: יְשָׁרִים, שֶׁחוֹרְצִים דָּבָר בַּאֲמִתּוֹ וּמִשְׁפָּטוֹ בְּלֹא עַוְלָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means the upright, who decide a matter by its truth and judge it without wrong.

10:8.headline: The babbling fool wears himself out, or stumbles
10:8.body: Rashi reads this rare verb as toil, citing the Sifrei, where the people complain 'how much we have toiled on the road'. Ibn Ezra reads it as stumbling, and Metzudat Zion gives both.

sources.quote: אָמְרוּ: כַּמָּה נִתְלַבַּטְנוּ בַדֶּרֶךְ
sources.says: Rashi says the word means weariness, and cites the Sifrei, where the people say 'how much we toiled on the road'.

sources.quote: ילבט - פירוש יכשל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means he will stumble.

sources.quote: ילבט. ענין עייפות וכשלון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means weariness and stumbling.

10:9.headline: The crooked man will be found out, or broken
10:9.body: יודע usually means 'will be known', and Ibn Ezra first reads it that way: his crookedness shows when he falls into trouble. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it as 'will be broken', citing a verse in Judges about the men of Sukkot.

sources.quote: הוא נודע לאחרים, שהוא מעקש דרכיו בנפלו ברעות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it becomes known to others that he twists his ways, when he falls into trouble.

sources.quote: פרוש אחר: יודע - ישבר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra gives a second reading: he will be broken.

sources.quote: יִשָּׁבֵר וְיִתְיַסֵּר
sources.says: Rashi says he will be broken and punished.

sources.quote: יודע. ענין שבירה כמו ויודע בהם אנשי סוכות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means breaking, as with the men of Sukkot in Judges.

10:11.headline: The same words twice: who covers whom?
10:11.body: The words ופי רשעים יכסה חמס appear in verse 6 and again here, and in verse 6 Rashi reads them as violence covering the mouth of the wicked and killing them. Here he says they mean something else: their smooth mouth hides the hatred in their heart.

sources.quote: הֶחָמָס יְכַסֶּה עַל פִּיהֶם וְיַהַרְגֵם
sources.says: On verse 6, Rashi says the violence will cover their mouth and kill them.

sources.quote: וְאֵין פִּתְרוֹן מִקְרָא זֶה דּוֹמֶה לְפִתְרוֹן הָעֶלְיוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says their mouth covers the violence in their heart, and that this verse is not explained like the one above.

10:16.headline: The wicked man's gain leads to sin, or to loss
10:16.body: חטאת usually means sin, and Ibn Ezra reads it that way. Metzudat Zion says it means falling short, from the root for missing a target, and Metzudat David says the wicked man's gains cut his life short.

sources.quote: הוא פרי מחשבותיו, שיחשוב לעשות חטאת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the wicked man's yield is the fruit of his thoughts, as he plans to sin.

sources.quote: לחטאת. ענין חסרון כמו קולע וכו׳ ולא יחטיא
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means lack, as in the slingers who would not miss.

sources.quote: פרי מעשה הרשע היא סיבה להחסיר ימי חייו
sources.says: Metzudat David says the fruit of the wicked man's deeds causes his days to be cut short.

10:18.headline: Slander, the talk that sets everyone murmuring
10:18.body: דבה means an evil report. Rashi and Metzudat Zion tie it to דובב, 'to murmur': it is talk that gets many people whispering about someone.

sources.quote: שֶׁיִּהְיוּ אֲנָשִׁים דּוֹבְבִין בּוֹ עַל חֲבֵירוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it is gossip that makes people murmur about his fellow.

sources.quote: ענין לעז והוצאת שם רע שרבים דובבים ומספרים בו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means spreading a bad name, which many murmur and tell about.

10:31.headline: The righteous mouth speaks wisdom, or bears it like fruit
10:31.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion tie this rare verb to ניב, speech, as in Isaiah's ניב שפתים. Ibn Ezra ties it to תנובה, produce: the mouth yields wisdom as a field yields crops.

sources.quote: פִּי צַדִּיק יָנוּב חָכְמָה. יְדַבֵּר
sources.says: Rashi says it means will speak, from ניב שפתים in Isaiah.

sources.quote: ינוב. ענין דבור כמו בורא ניב שפתים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means speech, as in Isaiah.

sources.quote: ינוב - מענין תנובה ופירוש יתן תנובת החכמה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it comes from תנובה, produce: the mouth gives the yield of wisdom.

11:7.headline: The hope of his 'strength': his sons, or his wrongdoing?
11:7.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion read אונים as strength, meaning the sons who come from a man's strength, so his children lose their hope when he dies. Ibn Ezra hears און, 'wrongdoing': the hopes of those who plan evil are lost.

sources.quote: תּוֹחֶלֶת בָּנָיו, שֶׁהֵם אוֹנוֹ, אָבְדָה
sources.says: Rashi says the hope of his sons, who are his strength, is lost.

sources.quote: אונים. בנים הבאים מכחו כמו כחי וראשית אוני
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they are sons who come from his strength, as in 'my strength and the first of my vigor'.

sources.quote: אונים - מן און, כלומר שיוחילו לעשות און
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it comes from און, wrongdoing: those who hope to do wrong.

11:13.headline: Maimonides uses this verse to explain why he keeps secrets
11:13.body: The verse warns against a gossip who tells secrets. Ralbag also reads it about the deep secrets of wisdom about God, and Maimonides quotes it to explain why he will not spell out the Sages' hints in full.

sources.quote: לכן לא אאריך בפירושן ולא אפשוט אותן, כדי שלא אהיה
sources.says: Maimonides says he will not explain the Sages' sayings at length, so as not to be a 'revealer of secrets'.

sources.quote: מי שהוא מגלה סוד החכמה בענינים האלהיים והעמוקים מאד הנה הוא מגונה כמו הולך רכיל
sources.says: Ralbag says one who reveals the secret of wisdom about divine and very deep matters is as bad as a gossip.

11:16.headline: A gracious woman holds on to honor, or to wealth
11:16.body: כבוד usually means honor. Ibn Ezra says here it likely means wealth, which the gracious woman keeps hold of, and Rashi reads her as the people of Israel drawing near to God's glory.

sources.quote: או כבוד רמז לממון והוא הנכון בעיני
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says כבוד may hint at money, and that this is the right reading in his eyes.

sources.quote: כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל תְּקָרֵב תָּמִיד לִכְבוֹד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְתוֹרָתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the people of Israel always draw near to the honor of God and His Torah.

11:17.headline: Cruel to his relatives, or to his own body?
11:17.body: Rashi reads שארו as relatives: the cruel man brings trouble on his own family. Metzudat Zion reads it as one's own flesh, and Ralbag says a man who torments his own body is cruel, against what God wants.

sources.quote: וְהָאַכְזָרִי הוּא עוֹכֵר אֶת קְרוֹבָיו
sources.says: Rashi says the cruel man troubles his relatives.

sources.quote: שארו. בשרו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means his flesh.

sources.quote: קצת האנשים יחשבו עבודה לשם יתב' מה שיענו גופם ענוי וזה הפך רצון הש"י
sources.says: Ralbag says some people think afflicting their bodies serves God, but it is the opposite of God's will.

11:18.headline: A true reward, or a dam that catches fish
11:18.body: Ibn Ezra reads שכר as the reward God gives. Rashi reads it as a dam: like a man who blocks a stream to catch fish, the one who sows charity can be sure of a full catch.

sources.quote: כְּאָדָם הַסּוֹכֵר אַמַּת הַמַּיִם כְּדֵי לִלְקוֹט דָּגִים, וּבָטוּחַ שֶׁיִּמְצָא שָׁם דָּגִים הַרְבֵּה
sources.says: Rashi says it is like a man who dams a water channel to gather fish and is sure to find many there.

sources.quote: שכרו שיתן לו השם הוא אמת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the reward God gives him is true.

11:21.headline: 'Hand to hand': whose hands are these?
11:21.body: Rashi reads it as payment passing from God's hand straight into the sinner's hand. Ibn Ezra sets God's hand against the evildoer's hand, and the Targum speaks of one who raises his hand against his friend.

sources.quote: מִיַּד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיָדוֹ תָּבוֹא לוֹ שְׂכַר פְּעֻלָּתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says from God's hand to his hand comes the payment for his deeds.

sources.quote: יד ליד - השם לנגד יד הרע
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says God's hand is set against the hand of the evildoer.

sources.quote: דְמוֹשִׁיט אַיְדָא עַל חַבְרֵיהּ לָא מִזְדַכֵּי מִן בִּישְׁתָּא
sources.says: The Targum says one who stretches out his hand against his friend will not be cleared of evil.

11:22.headline: 'Without taste' means without good sense
11:22.body: טעם usually means taste. Metzudat Zion says here it means sound judgment, and Rashi applies the verse to a scholar who turns away from the Torah, like a gold ring in a pig's snout.

sources.quote: טעם. עניינו העצה ותוכן הדבר כמו וטעם זקנים יקח
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means good counsel and the sense of a thing, as in 'He takes away the judgment of the elders'.

sources.quote: כֵּן תַּלְמִיד חָכָם הַסָּר מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ הַטּוֹבָה
sources.says: Rashi says it is like a Torah scholar who strays from the good path.

11:23.headline: The wicked hope to rage, or their hope ends in punishment
11:23.body: Ibn Ezra explains the word: anger that goes past its limit is called עברה, from עבר, to cross over, and the wicked hope for a chance to rage. Rashi reads it as where their hope leads: to punishment in Gehinnom.

sources.quote: ומדת הכעס שתעבור על מדה, תקרא עברה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says anger that passes beyond its measure is called עברה.

sources.quote: בְּטוּחִים וּמְקַוִּים לְגֵיהִנֹּם
sources.says: Rashi says they are sure of and headed for Gehinnom.

11:25.headline: One who waters others will be watered, or will learn
11:25.body: Rashi reads יורא as being filled with good in return. Ibn Ezra links it to teaching, and the Targum says plainly: one who teaches will also learn.

sources.quote: גַּם הוּא יוֹרֶא. יִשְׂבַּע טוֹב
sources.says: Rashi says he too will be filled with good.

sources.quote: יורא - מלשון והורית להם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word comes from 'and you shall teach them'.

sources.quote: וּמַן דִמְאַלֵף אַף הוּא יֵלִיף
sources.says: The Targum says one who teaches will also learn.

11:26.headline: Hoarding grain, or holding back Torah
11:26.body: בר is grain, and Ibn Ezra reads the verse about a man who hoards grain in a famine to sell it dear. Rashi reads it as Torah teaching, and Metzudat David says the verse is a parable for sharing wisdom.

sources.quote: מוֹנֵעַ בָּר. מְלַמֵּד תּוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi reads 'one who withholds grain' as being about teaching Torah.

sources.quote: והוא נאמר למשל על השפעת החכמה לזולת
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is said as a parable about giving wisdom to others.

sources.quote: מי שמונע בעת רעב תבואתו עד שימכרה בדמים יקרים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is one who holds back his grain in a famine until he can sell it at a high price.

11:27.headline: Seeking good, or rising at dawn to do it
11:27.body: שחר means to seek, as Metzudat Zion says. Ibn Ezra also hears שחר, 'dawn': a person who gets up early to do good.

sources.quote: שוחר. ענין דרישה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means seeking.

sources.quote: שוחר - שיקום בשחר לעשות טוב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is one who rises at dawn to do good.

11:29.headline: He who troubles his home inherits wind, or anger
11:29.body: Ibn Ezra reads רוח as wind and emptiness: the fool is left with nothing. Metzudat Zion reads it as anger, the quarreling that fills a home where there is not enough to eat.

sources.quote: באולתו הוא נוחל רוח והבל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says through his folly he inherits wind and emptiness.

sources.quote: רוח. עניינו כעס
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means anger.

sources.quote: הנה בזה יתרבה המריבה והכעס וכאלו ינחל לעצמו רוח הכעס
sources.says: Metzudat David says quarreling and anger grow, as if he inherits a spirit of anger.

11:30.headline: The wise 'take souls' by teaching them the good way
11:30.body: To 'take souls' could sound like killing. Rashi says the wise man gains souls by teaching them the good way, like the souls Abraham 'made' in Haran, and Ibn Ezra links לקח to teaching.

sources.quote: שֶׁמְּלַמְּדָם דֶּרֶךְ טוֹב, וַהֲרֵי הֵם לוֹ כְּאִלּוּ קְנָאָם
sources.says: Rashi says he teaches them the good way, and it is as if he acquired them.

sources.quote: ולוקח - מענין: כי לקח טוב. ופירש ומחכים נפשות חכם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it comes from 'good teaching', meaning the wise man makes souls wise.

12:1.headline: A boor is named with the word for cattle
12:1.body: בער means a fool. Metzudat Zion says the word comes from בעיר, cattle, as in 'we and our cattle' in Numbers, because a fool is like an animal.

sources.quote: בער. שוטה ע״ש שנמשל כבהמות והוא מל׳ אנחנו ובעירנו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a fool, named so because he is likened to beasts, from the word in 'we and our cattle'.

12:4.headline: A woman of valor: one who brings wealth, or works hard
12:4.body: Ibn Ezra reads חיל as wealth: a woman who brings in money is her husband's crown. Ralbag reads it as a woman who is quick and diligent in her work. The Targum calls her a worthy woman.

sources.quote: חיל - מן חילך פירוש ממון, כלומר האשה שתקנה ממון היא עטרת בעלה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says חיל means money: a woman who acquires wealth is her husband's crown.

sources.quote: הנה האשה הזריזה במעשיה היא עטרת בעלה
sources.says: Ralbag says the woman who is quick and diligent in her work is her husband's crown.

sources.quote: אִתְּתָא כְשַׁרְתָּא כְּלִילָא לְבַעֲלָהּ
sources.says: The Targum translates 'a worthy woman is a crown to her husband'.

12:8.headline: A twisted heart, or a heart that wanders
12:8.body: Rashi first compares נעוה to a verse in Isaiah where it means bent or twisted. He then offers a second root, נע, to wander: a heart that will not stay put. Metzudat Zion takes the second reading.

sources.quote: נַעֲוֵה. כְּמוֹ ״נַעֲוֵיתִי מִשְּׁמֹעַ״ (ישעיה כא:ג)
sources.says: Rashi compares the word to 'I am bent over so I cannot hear' in Isaiah.

sources.quote: וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר נַעֲוֵה – מִי שֶׁלִּבּוֹ נָעוּעַ, מִגִּזְרַת ״נָע וָנָד״
sources.says: Rashi says one can also read it as a person whose heart is unsteady, from the root of 'a wanderer and a drifter'.

sources.quote: ונעוה. מל׳ נע כאשר יאמר מן זע זעוה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from the root for moving, the way זעוה comes from זע.

12:10.headline: To know an animal's soul means to give it what it needs
12:10.body: Here ידע, to know, means to care for. Rashi says the righteous man knows what his animal and his household need. On Samuel, he uses this verse to show that 'you know your servant' means 'you gave me all I need'.

sources.quote: מַה בְּהֶמְתּוֹ וּבְנֵי בֵיתוֹ צְרִיכִים
sources.says: Rashi says the righteous man knows what his animal and his household need.

sources.quote: נָתַתָּ לִי כָּל צְרָכַי, כְּמוֹ (משלי יב:י): ״יוֹדֵעַ צַדִּיק נֶפֶשׁ בְּהֶמְתּוֹ״
sources.says: Rashi explains David's 'you know your servant' as 'you gave me all I need', like this verse.

12:10.headline: His animal may be the animal side of the man himself
12:10.body: Plainly, a good person cares for his animals. Ralbag reads 'his animal' as his own bodily side: a good person gives his body the food it truly needs to keep going.

sources.quote: והרצון בנפש בהמתו הנפש החמרית שהיא לאדם
sources.says: Ralbag says 'the soul of his animal' means the bodily soul a person has as an animal, not as a human.

12:12.headline: The wicked crave a hunter's catch, or a strong fortress
12:12.body: Rashi reads מצוד as hunting: the wicked want to live off what others catch by robbery. Metzudat Zion reads it as a fortress, as in Ezekiel.

sources.quote: מִמְּצוֹד רְשָׁעִים, שֶׁצָּדִין אֶת הַבְּרִיּוֹת בִּגְזֵלוֹת וְחָמָס
sources.says: Rashi says it is the catch of the wicked, who hunt people with robbery and violence.

sources.quote: מצוד. עניינו מבצר חזק כמו יבאוהו במצדות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a strong fortress, as in 'they brought him into strongholds'.

12:24.headline: The busy, the honest, or the owners of gold
12:24.body: Ibn Ezra reads חרוצים as people who keep moving to earn a living, or as owners of חרוץ, gold. Rashi reads it as the honest.

sources.quote: חרוצים - מן אז תחרץ שטעמו נוע, כלומר מתנועעים אחר מחייתם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word means moving: people who bustle about for their living.

sources.quote: ויתכן חרוצים, בעלי חרוץ והוא הזהב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it may also mean owners of חרוץ, which is gold.

sources.quote: יַד חָרֻצִים. יְשָׁרִים
sources.says: Rashi says it means the upright.

12:26.headline: The righteous man is above his friend, or gives way to him
12:26.body: Ibn Ezra reads יתר as having more: the righteous man is better than his fellow. Rashi reads it as letting go: the righteous man lets slights pass. Metzudat Zion notes the word carries both 'left over' and 'above'.

sources.quote: כלומר יש יתרון לצדיק יותר מרעהו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the righteous man has an advantage over his fellow.

sources.quote: הַצַּדִּיק מְוַתֵּר מִדּוֹתָיו וְעוֹבֵר עֲלֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the righteous man waives what is due to him and lets things pass.

sources.quote: כי כמו שמלת יותר היא משותפת להשארה וליתרון מעלה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word יותר is shared between 'remaining' and 'higher rank', and cites this verse.

12:27.headline: Precious gold, or an honest man's wealth
12:27.body: Metzudat Zion reads חרוץ as fine gold: a man's wealth is precious gold. Rashi reads it as an honest man: the money of an honest man is what is precious.

sources.quote: חרוץ. הוא מין זהב טוב כמו בירקרק חרוץ
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says חרוץ is a kind of fine gold.

sources.quote: מָמוֹן אָדָם כָּשֵׁר יָקָר הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says the money of an honest man is precious.

sources.quote: חָרוּץ. עוֹשֶׂה אֱמֶת
sources.says: Rashi says חרוץ means one who acts truthfully.

12:28.headline: Here אל means simply 'no': a path with no death
12:28.body: אל usually gives a command, 'do not'. Here it means plain 'not': the path of righteousness has no death. Rashi reads it so, and Ibn Ezra and Radak use this verse to show אל can mean 'not'.

sources.quote: אַל מָוֶת. לֹא יָמוּת
sources.says: Rashi says 'אל death' means he will not die.

sources.quote: והמדקדק שאמר שמלת אל לא תמצא כי אם על ציווי איננו נכון, והעד ודרך נתיבה אל מות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the grammarian who claimed אל appears only in commands is wrong, and this verse is the proof.

sources.quote: ויהיה פרוש ואל: ולא, כמו: ודרך נתיבה אל מות
sources.says: Radak says אל can mean 'and not', as in this verse.

13:6.headline: The verse calls the sinner 'sin' itself
13:6.body: חטאת normally means a sin. Rashi says here it stands for the sinner, named 'sin' because he is wholly wicked, and Ibn Ezra also reads it as a man of sin.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ חוֹטֵא, וְעַל שֶׁהוּא רָשָׁע גָּמוּר קוֹרְאֵהוּ חַטָּאת
sources.says: Rashi says the word means a sinner, and he is called 'sin' because he is wholly wicked.

sources.quote: ורשעה תסלף חטאת - איש חטאת ותעותהו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reads it as a man of sin, whom his wickedness twists.

13:7.headline: Pretending to be rich, or becoming rich later?
13:7.body: Rashi gives both senses of מתעשר: a man who shows himself as rich, or a man who starts with nothing and gets rich in the end. Ibn Ezra takes the second.

sources.quote: מַרְאֶה עַצְמוֹ עָשִׁיר
sources.says: Rashi's first reading: he shows himself to be rich.

sources.quote: יֵשׁ אָדָם שֶׁהוּא מִתְעַשֵּׁר בְּסוֹפוֹ, וְאֵין לוֹ כְּלוּם בִּתְחִלָּתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi's second reading: a man grows rich in the end though he had nothing at first.

sources.quote: מתעשר - שיעלה בעושר ולא היה לו כל מאומה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means he rises to wealth when he had nothing.

13:9.headline: The lamp of the wicked goes out by leaping
13:9.body: ידעך describes a flame going out. Rashi and Metzudat Zion say the root means to leap: the flame jumps off the wick and is cut off.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן קְפִיצָה, שֶׁהַשַּׁלְהֶבֶת קוֹפֶצֶת וְנִכְרֶתֶת
sources.says: Rashi says the word means leaping: the flame leaps and is cut off.

sources.quote: ענין ניתור וקפיצה וזהו כבוי הנר כי השלהבת קופצת מהפתילה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means jumping, and that is how a lamp goes out: the flame jumps off the wick.

13:10.headline: Here מצה means a quarrel, not unleavened bread
13:10.body: Rashi says מצה here means a quarrel. Metzudat Zion compares Isaiah 58:4, 'you fast for strife and quarrel' (לריב ומצה).

sources.quote: רַק בְּזָדוֹן יִתֵּן מַצָּה. מַחֲלֹקֶת
sources.says: Rashi explains מצה as a quarrel.

sources.quote: מצה. ענין מריבה כמו הן לריב ומצה תצומו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means strife, as in the Isaiah verse.

13:11.headline: Wealth from nothing, or learning crammed in bundles
13:11.body: On the plain reading, wealth that does not come from honest work shrinks. Rashi, following the Talmud, reads it as Torah study: one who crams learning in big bundles (חבילות) forgets it bit by bit.

sources.quote: עוֹשֶׂה גִּרְסָתוֹ חֲבִילוֹת חֲבִילוֹת יִמְעָט, שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּכַּח מִמֶּנּוּ מְעַט מְעַט
sources.says: Rashi says one who studies in large bundles will have less, because he forgets it little by little.

sources.quote: הון הבא מהבל ר״ל לא מיגיע כפים כ״א מגזל וחמס
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is wealth that comes not from hard work but from robbery.

13:12.headline: מחלה here is not 'illness' but 'makes sick'
13:12.body: מחלה can be a noun, illness, as in Exodus 23:25. Rashi says here it is a verb, 'brings sickness to the heart', and Ibn Ezra also reads it as a form that acts.

sources.quote: מְבִיאָה חוֹלִי לַלֵּב, וְאֵין מַחֲלָה זֶה שֵׁם דָּבָר
sources.says: Rashi says it brings sickness to the heart, and is not the noun 'illness' here.

sources.quote: מחלה - מפעלת פירוש מי שתוחלתו נמשכה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra calls מחלה an active form, about a person whose hope drags on.

13:13.headline: Scorning the word: a pledge taken, or a wound?
13:13.body: Rashi reads יחבל as being held in pledge: whoever scorns a word of Torah ends up owing for it. Metzudat Zion reads it as injury and a blow.

sources.quote: הַבּוֹזֶה אֶחָד מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, סוֹף מִתְמַשְׁכֵּן עָלָיו
sources.says: Rashi says one who scorns a word of Torah will in the end be held in pledge for it.

sources.quote: יחבל. מל׳ חבלה ומכה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from injury and a blow.

13:15.headline: The traitors' road is hard: hard to walk, or hard to change?
13:15.body: Ralbag says the traitors' road is איתן, hard to walk, like a rock face. Ibn Ezra says it is firm: a wise man cannot turn them off it.

sources.quote: ואולם דרך הבוגדים הוא איתן שיקשה ללכת בו כמו שן סלע ומצודה
sources.says: Ralbag says the traitors' road is hard to walk, like a crag of rock.

sources.quote: וחזק דרכם שהמשכיל לא יוכל להשיבם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says their way is strong, so the wise man cannot bring them back.

13:19.headline: A desire that comes true, or a desire that is broken?
13:19.body: Rashi reads נהיה as 'come to be': a wish that comes true is sweet. Metzudat Zion reads it as 'broken', as in Daniel 8:27, so the soul delights when bodily craving is broken.

sources.quote: כְּשֶׁבָּאָה תַּאֲוָתוֹ לוֹ לָאָדָם, הִיא עֲרֵבָה לְנַפְשׁוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says when a person's desire comes to him, it is sweet to his soul.

sources.quote: נהיה. ענין שבירה כמו נהיתי ונחליתי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means breaking, as in 'I was broken and sick' in Daniel.

sources.quote: כאשר נשברה תאות האדם בענייני הגוף אז תערב לנפש המשכלת
sources.says: Metzudat David says when a person's bodily desire is broken, it is sweet to the thinking soul.

13:23.headline: ראשים here means the poor, not heads
13:23.body: ראשים usually means heads or leaders, but Metzudat Zion says here it comes from רש, poor. Rashi agrees: much grain comes from the plowing of poor people.

sources.quote: ראשים. מלשון רש ועני
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from רש, poor.

sources.quote: הַרְבֵּה תְּבוּאָה בָּאָה לָעוֹלָם עַל יְדֵי נִיר אֲנָשִׁים דַּלִּים
sources.says: Rashi says much grain comes into the world through the plowing of poor people.

13:24.headline: Discipline him at dawn: every morning, or while young?
13:24.body: שחרו comes from שחר, dawn, and Rashi and Ibn Ezra read it as every morning. Metzudat Zion reads it as the dawn of life: discipline him while he is young.

sources.quote: תָּמִיד לַבְּקָרִים מְיַסְּרֵהוּ
sources.says: Rashi says he disciplines him every morning.

sources.quote: שחרו - ייסרהו בכל שחר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he disciplines him every dawn.

sources.quote: עניינו ימי הילדות שהוא בתחילת הימים והושאל מל׳ שחר הבקר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means the days of childhood, the start of life, borrowed from the word for morning dawn.

14:1.headline: Wisdom builds a house, or wise women do
14:1.body: Ibn Ezra reads חכמות as wisdom herself, who builds her house. Rashi says the vowel shows it is not the noun 'wisdom' but 'the wise among women', who keep their homes standing.

sources.quote: חָכְמוֹת נָקוּד פַּתָּח, שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֵׁם דָּבָר, אֶלָּא הַחֲכָמוֹת שֶׁבַּנָּשִׁים בּוֹנוֹת אֶת בָּתֵּיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the word has a patach vowel, so it is not a noun but means the wise women, who build their homes.

sources.quote: חכמות - החכמה היא תבנה ביתה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is wisdom that builds her house.

14:3.headline: A rod inside the fool's mouth: his tongue
14:3.body: חטר is a rare word for a rod or a shoot. Ibn Ezra says the rod is the tongue, which strikes with proud words, and Metzudat David says it is pride standing stiff like a stick.

sources.quote: חוטר. מטה כמו ויצא חוטר מגזע ישי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a rod, as in 'a shoot shall come out of the stump of Jesse'.

sources.quote: והוא רמז ללשון שנמשלה למטה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the rod hints at the tongue, which is compared to a rod that strikes with proud words.

sources.quote: גאוה זקופה כמקל
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is pride that stands upright like a stick.

14:4.headline: Not 'thousands' here, but oxen
14:4.body: אלפים usually means thousands. Metzudat Zion and Ibn Ezra say here it means oxen, as in 'the young of your cattle' in Deuteronomy.

sources.quote: אלפים. שורים כמו שגר אלפיך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means oxen, as in Deuteronomy 'the young of your cattle'.

sources.quote: אלפים - שוורים. וכן: ככבש אלוף
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means oxen, and compares a verse in Jeremiah.

14:4.headline: No oxen: an empty manger, or a full granary?
14:4.body: בר can mean clean or grain. Rashi reads it as clean, so without oxen the manger is empty, while Ralbag reads it as grain: without oxen the stores stay full, but big harvests need an ox's strength.

sources.quote: בָּר. נָקִי וְרֵיקָם
sources.says: Rashi says it means clean and empty.

sources.quote: כשלא ימצאו שורים ימצאו אוצרות התבואה שאוכלים השורים מלאים בר
sources.says: Ralbag says that when there are no oxen, the stores of grain the oxen would eat stay full.

sources.quote: באין שוורים יש אבוס אחד מן בר, מענין לשבור בר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra gives both readings, the second taking בר as grain, as in 'to buy grain'.

14:9.headline: The guilt offering speaks up for fools, or fools mock it
14:9.body: יליץ can come from מליץ, an advocate, or from לץ, a scoffer. Rashi reads it as the fools' guilt payment pleading for them, while Ibn Ezra also offers that fools mock the guilt offering and say it does nothing.

sources.quote: וְיָלִיץ בַּעֲדָם אֲשָׁמָם, שֶׁהֵם מְבִיאִים מְמוֹנָם לוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says their guilt payment speaks up for them when they bring their money to the one they wronged.

sources.quote: יליץ. מל׳ מליצה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from pleading or speaking for someone.

sources.quote: כשיעשה אשם יתלוצץ ואומר שאינו מועיל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra gives another reading: when the fool brings a guilt offering he mocks it and says it does no good.

14:14.headline: A heart that turns back, or a heart full of dross
14:14.body: Metzudat Zion and Ibn Ezra read סוג as turning away. Rashi reads it as dross, like silver mixed with waste, and so a wicked person.

sources.quote: סוג. עניינו החזרה לאחור כמו והוסג אחור משפט
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means turning back, as in Isaiah 'justice is turned back'.

sources.quote: סוג פעול על משקל מול וענינו סור
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word means turned away.

sources.quote: סוּג הוּא שֵׁם הַפְּסֹלֶת, סוּג הוּא הַכֶּסֶף הַמְעֻרְבָּב בַּפְּסֹלֶת
sources.says: Rashi says סוג is the name for waste, silver mixed with dross, so it means a wicked person.

14:14.headline: Three readings of מעליו: above, apart, or from leaves
14:14.body: Rashi reads מעליו as the good man standing above the wicked, and Metzudat David reads it as the good man parting from him. Ibn Ezra hears עלה, a leaf: the good man is filled even by his small deeds, the leaves, as well as his great ones, the fruit.

sources.quote: וּמִמַּעַל לוֹ לָרָשָׁע, יִהְיֶה הַצַּדִּיק
sources.says: Rashi says the righteous man will be above the wicked one.

sources.quote: יהיה איש טוב נפרד מעליו לבל יהיה נלקה עמו
sources.says: Metzudat David says the good man will be parted from him, so he is not struck along with him.

sources.quote: ומעליו - מן עלה זית, ודימה מעשיו הטובים במצות הקלות בעלים והחמורות בפרי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word comes from 'olive leaf', comparing light commandments to leaves and weighty ones to fruit.

14:16.headline: The fool trusts himself, or slips and falls
14:16.body: בוטח usually means 'trusts', and Metzudat David reads it that way: the fool is sure no harm will come. Rashi reads it as slipping and falling, citing a verse in Jeremiah and its Aramaic translation.

sources.quote: וּמַחֲלִיק וְנוֹפֵל בָּאָרֶץ
sources.says: Rashi says it means he slips and falls to the ground, and notes that some explain it as real trust.

sources.quote: ובוטח בעצמו שלא יאונה לו רעה
sources.says: Metzudat David says the fool trusts himself that no harm will come to him.

14:17.headline: A man of schemes, or a man who overthinks
14:17.body: Rashi reads מזמות as plotting evil. Ralbag reads it as thinking too long about whether to act at all, which makes people hate dealing with him.

sources.quote: מַחֲשָׁבוֹת עֵצָה רָעָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means thoughts of evil counsel.

sources.quote: שחושב מחשבות רבות וזמן ארוך אם ראוי לעשות הדברים אם לא הנה ישנא
sources.says: Ralbag says it is one who thinks many thoughts for a long time about whether to act, and so he is hated.

14:18.headline: The shrewd crown themselves with knowledge, or wait for it
14:18.body: Rashi and Metzudat David read יכתרו from כתר, a crown: the shrewd make knowledge a crown for their heads. Ralbag reads it as waiting: the wise hold back until knowledge is clear to them.

sources.quote: יַעֲשׂוּהוּ כֶּתֶר לְרֹאשָׁם
sources.says: Rashi says they make it a crown for their head.

sources.quote: אוחזים בדעת ועושים אותם כתר לראשם
sources.says: Metzudat David says they hold on to knowledge and make it a crown for their head.

sources.quote: ואמנם החכמים ימתינו שימצאו הדעת
sources.says: Ralbag says the wise wait until they find knowledge.

14:29.headline: The hot-tempered man raises folly, or takes it as his share
14:29.body: Ibn Ezra and Metzudat David read מרים as 'lifts up': anger raises folly above wisdom. Rashi reads it as 'sets it apart for his share', so the hot-tempered man picks folly as his portion.

sources.quote: כי מאריך אפו ישפיל האולת וזה ירימה בהתכעסו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the patient man lowers folly, and the angry man raises it.

sources.quote: הוא מרים האולת על התבונה
sources.says: Metzudat David says he raises folly over understanding.

sources.quote: מֵרִים אִוֶּלֶת. מַפְרִישָׁהּ לְחֶלְקוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says he sets folly apart as his portion.

14:30.headline: A healing heart, or a relaxed heart, gives the body life
14:30.body: Rashi reads מרפא as healing: a heart that cures ill will and lets things go. Metzudat Zion reads it as slack and calm, though spelled with an aleph, and Metzudat David says such a heart holds no grudge.

sources.quote: לֵב בָּשָׂר, שֶׁהוּא רוֹפֵא אֶת הָרָעָה וְעוֹבֵר עַל מִדּוֹתָיו
sources.says: Rashi says it is a heart of flesh that heals the bad and lets offenses pass.

sources.quote: מרפא. מל׳ רפיון עם שהוא באל״ף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from slackening, even though it is spelled with an aleph.

sources.quote: מי שיש לו לב רפוי ואינו מקשה לבו לנטור קנאה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is one whose heart is relaxed and who does not harden it to hold a grudge.

14:33.headline: Among fools, wisdom announces itself, or is taught to them
14:33.body: Rashi says a fool's little wisdom shouts itself out, as the Talmud says: one coin in a jar rattles 'kish kish'. Ibn Ezra reads it as the wise man making wisdom known to fools, hoping they will learn.

sources.quote: מְעַט חָכְמָה שֶׁבְּלִבּוֹ מַכְרִיזָה; אִיסְתְּרָא בְּלָגִינָא קִישׁ קִישׁ קָרְיָא
sources.says: Rashi says the little wisdom in his heart announces itself, like one coin in a jar that rattles.

sources.quote: תודע - יודיעה להם אולי ילמדוה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the wise man makes it known to them, in case they learn it.

15:1.headline: Anger is called 'nose' because it rises up into the face
15:1.body: אף means nose, and here it means anger. Ibn Ezra stops on why: in a rage, anger climbs up and shows in a person's nose, so the verse says it 'rises'.

sources.quote: כי מדת הכעס בעת הזעף תעלה ותראה באפי האדם, על כן נקרא הזעף אף
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says anger rises and shows in a person's nose, and that is why rage is called אף.

15:2.headline: A fool's talk gushes like a spring that never stops
15:2.body: יביע is a word for speaking taken from a flowing spring. The commentators stop on the picture: folly pours out of a fool's mouth without a break.

sources.quote: והוא מושאל ממעיין הנובע מים רבים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means speaking, borrowed from a spring that pours out much water.

sources.quote: מנחל נובע, כלומר לא תפסק האולת מפיהם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it comes from a flowing stream: the folly never stops coming out of their mouths.

15:4.headline: A healing tongue, or a soft one?
15:4.body: מרפא can come from רפא, to heal, or from רפה, to be soft. Ibn Ezra reads a tongue whose teaching heals foolishness. Metzudat Zion and Ralbag read a soft tongue that speaks gently.

sources.quote: רמז למוסר שירפא נגע הסכלות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it hints at teaching that heals the sickness of foolishness.

sources.quote: מרפא. מלשון רפיון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from softness.

sources.quote: מי שנותן רפיון לשונו ורפות דברים יגרום לעצמו החיים
sources.says: Ralbag says one who keeps his tongue soft and speaks gently brings life to himself.

15:4.headline: Broken by a storm wind, or broken in what he wants?
15:4.body: רוח can mean wind, and it can mean will. Rashi reads twisted speech bringing ruin like the east wind. Metzudat Zion reads רוח as will: the twisted speaker never gets what he wants.

sources.quote: סוֹפָהּ לְהָבִיא עָלָיו שֶׁבֶר הַבָּא בְּרוּחַ קָדִים
sources.says: Rashi says twisted speech ends by bringing on the speaker a breaking that comes with the east wind.

sources.quote: ברוח. עניינו רצון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says רוח here means will.

sources.quote: בא שבר ברצונו כי לא יקובל דבריו ולא ימולא רצונו
sources.says: Metzudat David says his will is broken: his words are not accepted and his wish is not met.

15:6.headline: The wicked man's crops, or the wicked man coming in?
15:6.body: תבואה usually means crops, and Ibn Ezra reads it that way. Metzudat Zion reads it from בוא, to come: when a wicked man comes into the house, it is spoiled. Rashi reads it as the idol King Manasseh brought into the Temple.

sources.quote: יש תבואה נעכרת, כענין זרעו חטים וקוצים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some crops are spoiled, like sowing wheat and reaping thorns.

sources.quote: ובתבואת. מל׳ ביאה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from 'coming'.

sources.quote: בעת בוא בו הרשע נשחת הבית ההוא
sources.says: Metzudat David says that when the wicked man comes into it, the house is ruined.

sources.quote: וּבַהֲבָאַת הַצֶּלֶם שֶׁהֵבִיא מְנַשֶּׁה
sources.says: Rashi says it means the idol Manasseh brought in, which spoiled the Temple.

15:7.headline: The wise crown knowledge, or scatter it?
15:7.body: יזרו can come from זר, a crown, or from זרה, to scatter. Rashi says the lips of the wise crown knowledge. Metzudat Zion and Metzudat David say they spread it, teaching it to everyone.

sources.quote: יַכְתִּירוּ דַעַת, כְּמוֹ ״זֵר זָהָב״
sources.says: Rashi says they crown knowledge, from זר as in 'a crown of gold'.

sources.quote: ענין פזור כמו יזורה על נוהו גפרית
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means scattering, as in Job 18:15.

sources.quote: המה מפזרים את הדעת ללמד לכל
sources.says: Metzudat David says they spread knowledge to teach everyone.

15:15.headline: Poor in money, or poor in spirit and mind?
15:15.body: עני usually means poor. Rashi reads it that way: even a poor man's Sabbaths and holidays are bad days. Ibn Ezra and Ralbag read it as someone sad, or poor in understanding, whose days are bad whatever he owns.

sources.quote: וַאֲפִלּוּ שַׁבָּתוֹת וְיָמִים טוֹבִים
sources.says: Rashi says all a poor man's days are bad, even Sabbaths and holidays.

sources.quote: תאר והוא המתעצב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word describes a person who is sad.

sources.quote: כל מי שהוא עני בדעות כל ימיו הם רעים
sources.says: Ralbag says anyone poor in understanding has bad days all his life.

15:17.headline: A meal named for the road it is carried on
15:17.body: ארחה is a meal. Ibn Ezra ties it to ארח, a road: a portion carried along to someone, the way a sent gift is named for sending. Metzudat Zion says it means a regular daily meal.

sources.quote: בעבור הנושאה עלי אורח, כמו שלוחים מן ישלח
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the meal is named for the one who carries it on the road, just as 'sent gifts' come from 'send'.

sources.quote: ענין האכילה התמידית בכל יום
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means the regular meal eaten every day.

15:22.headline: Counsel is called 'secret', or tied to 'foundation'
15:22.body: סוד here means counsel. Metzudat Zion gives two reasons for the word: advice is usually kept secret, or advice holds up an action the way a foundation, יסוד, holds up a building.

sources.quote: ענין עצה שדרכו להיות בסוד לבל יודע, או שהעצה הוא למעשה כיסוד לבנין
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says counsel is usually kept secret, or that counsel is to an action what a foundation is to a building.

15:30.headline: Light for the eyes: a lovely view, or Torah?
15:30.body: מאור עינים is literally 'light of the eyes'. Rashi first reads it as Torah, then plainly as a sight that delights, like a green garden and flowing rivers. Metzudat David reads it as the light of clearing up a doubt.

sources.quote: מְאוֹר עֵינַיִם. בַּתּוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi says the light of the eyes is in Torah.

sources.quote: כְּגוֹן גַּן יָרָק וּנְהָרוֹת הַמּוֹשְׁכִים
sources.says: Rashi says by the plain sense it is a sight the eyes enjoy, like a green garden and flowing rivers.

sources.quote: כי אין בעולם שמחה כהתרת הספקות
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is light shed on a doubtful matter, since no joy equals solving doubts.

16:2.headline: God weighs the spirits, or God is inside them
16:2.body: The root of ותכן usually means to weigh, and Rashi reads it as God counting up hearts, good and bad. Metzudat Zion and Metzudat David tie it to תוך, 'inside': God is within every person's spirit.

sources.quote: וּמוֹנֶה הַלְּבָבוֹת, מִי הַטּוֹב וּמִי הָרָע
sources.says: Rashi says God counts the hearts, who is good and who is bad.

sources.quote: ותוכן. מל׳ תוך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from תוך, 'inside'.

sources.quote: ה׳ הוא בתוך רוחו של כל אדם ויודע הוא אם דרכיו זכאים אם לא
sources.says: Metzudat David says God is inside every person's spirit and knows whether his ways are clean.

16:3.headline: Roll your deeds onto God, or reveal them to Him
16:3.body: גל means to roll, and Rashi reads it as rolling your needs onto God and letting Him carry them. The Aramaic Targum reads it as גלי, 'reveal your deeds to God'.

sources.quote: גַּלְגֵּל וְהַשְׁלֵךְ עָלָיו צְרָכֶיךָ
sources.says: Rashi says roll and throw your needs onto God; another reading is to pray to Him for all your needs.

sources.quote: גְלִי לֶאֱלָהָא עוֹבְדָךְ
sources.says: The Targum translates 'reveal your deeds to God'.

16:4.headline: God made everything for a purpose, but whose purpose?
16:4.body: למענהו means 'for his sake', and the commentators ask whose sake. Rashi ties it to ענה, to sing or testify, so everything exists to praise God, while Maimonides says 'his' may point to the thing made or to God's own will.

sources.quote: הַכֹּל עָשָׂה בִּשְׁבִיל קִלּוּסוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says God made everything for His praise, and offers a second reading: so that His work testifies to His power.

sources.quote: בגלל עצמותו יתעלה, כלומר רצונו, כי הוא עצמותו
sources.says: Maimonides says the ending may refer to the thing made, or to God, meaning for the sake of His will.

16:10.headline: The word for divining becomes praise for a king's rulings
16:10.body: קסם is the word for divining, as in the banned practices of Deuteronomy 18. Here it praises a king, so the commentators stop on it: they read it as a comparison, a king's ruling as firm and clear as an oracle's.

sources.quote: קסם. ענין ניחוש כמו קוסם קסמים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means divination, as in 'one who divines' in Deuteronomy 18.

sources.quote: כקסם שהוא דבר גזור, כן יאות להיות על שפתי מלך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word for 'like' is missing: just as divination is a fixed decree, so should a king's words be.

sources.quote: אמרי המלך ברורים כאלו היה קסם על שפתיו
sources.says: Metzudat David says the king's words are as clear as if he had divination on his lips.

16:14.headline: A wise man does not atone for anger, he wipes it away
16:14.body: The root כפר usually means to atone, but Rashi reads it here as calming the king. Metzudat Zion says the root means wiping off, which is why the Temple bowls are called כפורי: the priest wiped his hand on their rim.

sources.quote: יְכַפְּרֶנָּה. יְפַיְּסֶנָּה
sources.says: Rashi says it means he will calm the king's anger.

sources.quote: כי הכהן מקנח ידו מן הדם בשפת המזרק
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the root means removing and wiping, and the bowls got the name because the priest wiped the blood off his hand on their rim.

16:18.headline: Before a fall comes pride, or a rise to power
16:18.body: גאון usually means pride, and Ralbag reads it that way: pride causes the fall. Metzudat Zion says it means rule, and Metzudat David reads the verse as power coming first, so the fall hurts twice as much.

sources.quote: הנה הגאוה והגאון וגובה הרוח הוא סבה אל השבר ואל הכשלון
sources.says: Ralbag says pride and haughtiness are the cause of the breaking and the stumbling.

sources.quote: גאון. ענינו ממשלה כמו גאון יעקב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means rule, as in 'the pride of Jacob' in Amos.

sources.quote: בא לו מתחלה גאון וממשל רב כי בזה יכפל הצער
sources.says: Metzudat David says the wicked first gets greatness and wide rule, so that his pain is doubled when he falls.

16:20.headline: Happy is he, or these are his steps
16:20.body: אשריו usually means 'happy is he', and Ibn Ezra keeps that sense: he will be happy as his good grows. Rashi reads it as אשוריו, 'his steps', for the man who weighs his paths.

sources.quote: אַשְׁרָיו. הֵן אֲשׁוּרָיו שֶׁלּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the word means 'these are his steps'.

sources.quote: שיהא מאושר ברבות טובתו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means he will be made happy as his good increases.

16:21.headline: Sweet speech adds learning, and also wins people over
16:21.body: לקח comes from 'to take' and can mean a lesson, and Rashi and the Targum read it as learning gained from sweet teaching. Ralbag adds that sweet words draw people in and take hold of them.

sources.quote: כְּשֶׁאָדָם מַטְעִים דְּבָרָיו לְתַלְמִיד וּמַמְתִּיק דְּבָרָיו בִּטְעָמִים
sources.says: Rashi says that when a person explains and sweetens his words with reasons for a student, he adds learning.

sources.quote: מוֹסִיף אוּלְפָנָא
sources.says: The Targum translates 'adds teaching'.

sources.quote: ערבות הדברים ומתיקות' ימשוך הנפשות ויקחם
sources.says: Ralbag says pleasant, sweet words draw people's souls and take them.

16:22.headline: Fools are punished by their folly, or learn only from it
16:22.body: מוסר can mean punishment or a lesson, and Rashi reads it as the suffering fools bring on themselves through their folly. Ralbag reads it as the only lesson fools learn comes from their own mistakes.

sources.quote: יִסּוּרֵי אֱוִילִים עַל יְדֵי אִוֶּלֶת בָּאִים לָהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the suffering of fools comes to them through their folly.

sources.quote: ואולם האוילים לא יקנו מוסר כי אם מהאולת
sources.says: Ralbag says fools gain a lesson only from their folly.

16:26.headline: His mouth pushes him to work, or he bends his mouth
16:26.body: אכף appears only here, and Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it as forcing: hunger drives a man to toil. Ralbag reads it as bending: the man held back his appetite so he could toil for wisdom.

sources.quote: כְּשֶׁפִּיהוּ כּוֹפֵהוּ וְתוֹבֵעַ לוֹ מַאֲכָל
sources.says: Rashi says his mouth forces him and demands food.

sources.quote: אכף. מלשון כפיה ונגישה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means forcing and pressing.

sources.quote: כאשר כבש תאו' פיהו למזונות ולמשקים הערבים
sources.says: Ralbag reads it as the man subduing his mouth's appetite for tasty food and drink, so it does not keep him from seeking wisdom.

16:28.headline: The grumbler drives away a friend, a ruler, or God
16:28.body: אלוף can mean a close friend or a chief, and the Targum says 'his friend' while Metzudat Zion says a ruler. Rashi, following Bereshit Rabbah, says the grumbler drives away the Master of the world.

sources.quote: וְחַרְתָּנָא מַעֲרִיק רָחֲמֵיהּ
sources.says: The Targum translates 'the grumbler drives away his friend'.

sources.quote: אלוף. שר כמו ואל תבטחו באלוף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means a ruler.

sources.quote: מַפְרִיד מִמֶּנּוּ אַלּוּפוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
sources.says: Rashi says that through his complaining he drives away from himself the Master of the world.

16:30.headline: He winks his eyes, or shuts them to plot
16:30.body: This verb appears only here, and Rashi and the Targum read it as winking. Metzudat Zion reads it as shutting, and Metzudat David says the plotter closes his eyes so what he sees will not distract him.

sources.quote: עוֹצֶה עֵינָיו. לְשׁוֹן קְרִיצָה
sources.says: Rashi says the word means winking.

sources.quote: רָמַז בְּעַיְנוֹי
sources.says: The Targum translates 'signals with his eyes'.

sources.quote: עוצה. ענין סתימה כמו ויעצם את עיניכם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means shutting, as in Isaiah's 'He has shut your eyes'.

sources.quote: דרך המעמיק לחשוב מה יסתום אז עיניו לבל יבלבלו אותו דברים הנראים
sources.says: Metzudat David says one who thinks hard shuts his eyes so that things he sees do not confuse him.

17:1.headline: Dry bread, or a ruined Temple?
17:1.body: חרבה here means dry: a dry crust eaten in peace. Rashi hears the root of ruin in it: God preferred to destroy His house and be at peace from Israel's sins, rather than keep a house full of quarrelsome offerings.

sources.quote: חרבה. יבשה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means dry.

sources.quote: טוֹב הָיָה לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחֲרִיב בֵּיתוֹ וְעִירוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it was better for God to destroy His house and His city and be at peace from Israel's sins.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיוּ מַקְרִיבִין זִבְחֵי רִיב בְּבֵיתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the house full of quarrelsome sacrifices is God's house, where such offerings were brought.

17:8.headline: Who owns a bribe, the giver or the taker?
17:8.body: Ibn Ezra says the bribe's 'owner' is the giver, because taking a bribe is forbidden, so the taker cannot be called its owner. Metzudat David and the Targum say it is the one who receives it.

sources.quote: כן יש חן לשוחד בעיני בעליו והוא הנותן, כי בעבור שהוא אסור לקחתו לא יקרא הלוקח בעליו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the bribe's owner is the giver, since taking it is forbidden and the taker is not called its owner.

sources.quote: השוחד הוא בעיני בעליו המקבלם
sources.says: Metzudat David says the owner is the one who receives the bribe.

sources.quote: בְאַפֵּי מַאן דְשָׁקֵל לָהּ
sources.says: The Targum translates 'in the eyes of the one who takes it'.

17:9.headline: Bringing up a wrong again, or doing it again
17:9.body: שנה can mean to repeat or to do a second time, and Rashi reads it as one who holds a grudge and keeps bringing up an old wrong. Ibn Ezra reads it as sinning against the friend a second time.

sources.quote: שֶׁנּוֹטֵר אֵיבָה וּמַזְכִּירוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it is one who holds a grudge and reminds the other of what he did.

sources.quote: ושונה בדבר - לפשוע פעם אחרת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means to sin another time.

sources.quote: ושונה. מל׳ שנית
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from 'a second time'.

17:9.headline: Holding a grudge drives away a friend, a ruler, or God
17:9.body: אלוף can mean a close friend or a chief, and the Targum says 'friend' while Metzudat Zion says a ruler. Rashi says it is God, the Master of the world, who commanded 'do not bear a grudge'.

sources.quote: מְפָרֵק רָחֲמָא
sources.says: The Targum translates 'separates a friend'.

sources.quote: אלוף. שר ומושל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means a prince and ruler.

sources.quote: אָז מַפְרִיד מִמֶּנּוּ אַלּוּפוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם שֶׁהוּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says he drives away the Master of the world, God, who warned 'do not take revenge or bear a grudge'.

17:10.headline: An unusual stress turns תחת into the dread of rebuke
17:10.body: תחת usually means 'under' or 'instead of', but Rashi notes the stress here falls on its first letter, unlike anywhere else in the Bible. So he reads it as a noun like חתת, dread, and Metzudat Zion too reads it as fear and breaking.

sources.quote: תַּחַת זוֹ טַעֲמוֹ לְמַעְלָה בַּתָּי״ו, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּכָל הַמִּקְרָא
sources.says: Rashi says this word is stressed on the first letter, unlike anywhere else in Scripture, so it is a noun like חתת.

sources.quote: תחת. ענין פחד ושבר כמו אל תערוץ ואל תחת
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means fear and breaking, as in 'do not be afraid or dismayed' in Joshua.

sources.quote: יש אומרים: מן תנחת עלי ידך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports that some derive it from the root of 'Your hand came down on me', and calls that far-fetched.

17:16.headline: The fool has no heart: no will, or no mind?
17:16.body: לב, heart, can mean will or understanding, and Rashi reads it as no heart to keep what he learns, since he studies only to make a name. Metzudat David and Maimonides read it as having no capacity to understand.

sources.quote: וְאֵין בְּלִבּוֹ לְקַיְּמָהּ, וְאֵינוֹ לוֹמֵד תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא לִקְנוֹת שֵׁם
sources.says: Rashi says he has no intent to keep the Torah he learns, and studies only to win a name.

sources.quote: הלא אין לו לב משיג דברים מושכלים
sources.says: Metzudat David says the fool has no heart that can grasp ideas.

sources.quote: אבל אינו מבין אף מושכל, גם לא הקרוב למושכלות הראשונים
sources.says: Maimonides applies the verse to a person who cannot grasp even the simplest ideas, whom no strategy can help.

17:17.headline: A brother is born for hard times, or hard times are born
17:17.body: Rashi reads 'is born' as: in trouble a friend becomes like a brother to you. Ibn Ezra ties the word to the trouble that is born, meaning arises, and Maimonides lists this borrowed use of 'born' for events that come about in time.

sources.quote: לְעֵת הַצָּרָה יִוָּלֵד לְךָ הָרֵעַ כְּאָח
sources.says: Rashi says that in a time of trouble your friend is born to you like a brother, to help you.

sources.quote: ואח אוהב לעת צרה הנולדת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says a brother loves at the time of the trouble that is born, and notes the word should properly have been תולד.

sources.quote: והושאל גם כן למאורעות המתחדשים בזמן, כאילו הם דברים שנולדו
sources.says: Maimonides says the word 'born' is also borrowed for events that arise in time, as if they were born.

17:22.headline: A glad heart brings healing, or a shining face
17:22.body: גהה appears only here, and Metzudat Zion and Ibn Ezra read it as healing, with the word 'like' left out. Rashi reads the verse as a glad person's face shining.

sources.quote: ועניינו רפואה כמו ולא יגהה מכם מזור
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means healing, as in Hosea 'nor will He heal your wound'.

sources.quote: הלב שהוא שמח בחלקו ייטיב לגוף כגהה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says a heart content with its lot does the body good like medicine.

sources.quote: כְּשֶׁהָאָדָם שָׂמֵחַ בְּחֶלְקוֹ, פָּנָיו מְאִירִין
sources.says: Rashi says that when a person is happy with his lot, his face shines.

17:23.headline: Rashi turns the wicked man's bribe into a quiet plea
17:23.body: The plain sense is a judge taking a bribe in secret, as Ralbag reads it. Rashi stops on the word and reads it as God accepting humble words from the wicked in private, and turning their judgment from bad to good.

sources.quote: שיקח אותו בצנעא בדרך שלא יודע ויקחהו להטות ארחות משפט
sources.says: Ralbag says the wicked man takes the bribe in secret so it is not known, to bend the paths of justice.

sources.quote: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי הַכְנָעָה וּפִיּוּס מֵחֵיק הָרְשָׁעִים
sources.says: Rashi says God accepts words of submission and appeasement from the wicked, in private.

sources.quote: לַהֲפֹךְ דִּינוֹ מֵרָעָה לְטוֹבָה
sources.says: Rashi says this is to turn the person's judgment from bad to good.

17:28.headline: A silent fool seems wise, or one who silences a fool
17:28.body: מחריש can mean 'keeps silent' or 'makes silent', and the Targum reads it as a quiet fool being thought wise. Metzudat David reads it as anyone who can silence a fool being counted wise.

sources.quote: וְאַף שַׁטְיָא דְשָׁתֵק חַכִּימָא הוּא מִתְחַשֵׁב
sources.says: The Targum translates 'even a fool who is silent is counted wise'.

sources.quote: מי שיוכל להשתיק גם את האויל שלא יוסיף לדבר אולתו
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is one who can silence even a fool, so he speaks no more folly.

18:1.headline: The one who leaves: a deserter, or a seeker of wisdom?
18:1.body: Rashi reads נפרד as a man who cuts himself off from God to chase his desires, and the Sages name Lot, who left Abraham. Ibn Ezra reads the same man kindly: he leaves home because he longs to learn.

sources.quote: מִי שֶׁהוּא נִפְרָד מֵהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמֹר מִצְווֹתָיו
sources.says: Rashi says it is someone who separates from God and does not keep His commandments.

sources.quote: בְּלוֹט שֶׁנִּפְרַד מֵאַבְרָהָם עַל תַּאֲוַת לִבּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the Sages applied it to Lot, who left Abraham out of desire.

sources.quote: והנפרד ממקומו לבקש חכמה, בעבור תאוה שיתאוה ללמוד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is one who leaves his place to seek wisdom because he longs to learn.

18:1.headline: Torah is called תושיה because it always exists
18:1.body: Metzudat Zion says תושיה is a name for the Torah. He hears in it the word יש, 'there is', because the Torah lasts forever and never returns to nothing.

sources.quote: תושיה. כן נקראת התורה והוא מל׳ יש כי ישנה לעולם ולא תשוב לאין
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the Torah is called this, from the word יש, because it exists forever and does not return to nothing.

18:1.headline: His shame is exposed, or he mingles with the wise
18:1.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion read יתגלע as יתגלה, 'is revealed': the deserter's disgrace comes out among the wise. Ibn Ezra reads it as 'mixes in': the seeker joins every circle of learning.

sources.quote: יתגלע. כמו יתגלה בה״א
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is like יתגלה, 'is revealed', spelled with a ה.

sources.quote: בֵּין חֲכָמִים תִּגָּלֶה חֶרְפָּתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says his disgrace will be revealed among the wise.

sources.quote: ובכל אנשי תושיה יתערב וילך עמם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he mixes in with all people of wisdom and goes with them.

18:4.headline: Rashi: in Scripture, איש always means a strong man
18:4.body: איש is the everyday word for 'man'. Rashi stops on it and says that wherever Scripture uses it, it means a mighty man, great in strength.

sources.quote: כָּל אִישׁ שֶׁבַּמִּקְרָא לְשׁוֹן גִּבּוֹר גָּדוֹל בִּגְבוּרָה הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says every איש in Scripture means a hero, great in strength.

18:8.headline: A gossip's words are like blows, or like secrets
18:8.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion read כמתלהמים as crushing blows, Metzudat Zion saying it is הלום, 'strike', with its letters swapped. Ibn Ezra reads it as words hidden and covered, the whispers of a talebearer.

sources.quote: כמתלהמים. ענין הכאה המשברת והוא הפוך מן הלום
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a breaking blow, a reversed form of הלום, to strike.

sources.quote: דִּבְרֵי נִרְגָּן כְּמִתְלַהֲמִים. מַהֲלוּמוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says it means blows.

sources.quote: כמתלהמים כדברים מסותרים ומתכסין מן דברי הרכיל שידברם בסתר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means hidden, covered words, the gossip a talebearer speaks in secret.

18:16.headline: A gift that makes room: charity, or a bribe?
18:16.body: Ibn Ezra hears a bribe that gets a man out of trouble with the powerful. Rashi brings a reading about charity: giving widens a person's share in the world to come.

sources.quote: ומתן - רמז לשחד שיתן יוציאהו למרחב מצרתו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it hints at a bribe that brings the giver out of his trouble.

sources.quote: בְּנוֹתְנֵי צְדָקָה מְדַבֵּר, שֶׁמַּרְחִיב לוֹ חֶלְקוֹ לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא
sources.says: Rashi brings the midrash that it speaks of those who give charity, whose share in the world to come is widened.

19:6.headline: Not 'many' but 'the great' court the generous man
19:6.body: רבים usually means many. Metzudat Zion and Ibn Ezra read it as nobles, as in 'the king's great men' in Jeremiah, so even important people seek a generous man's favor.

sources.quote: רבים. גדולים וחשובים כמו רבי המלך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means great and important people, as in 'the king's officers'.

sources.quote: רבים - מן רבי המלך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word is like 'the king's great men', so the great seek the generous man's face.

19:7.headline: Written 'not', read 'to him': Rashi uses both
19:7.body: The word is written לא, 'not', but read לו, 'to him'. Rashi reads the poor man's claims as empty words, and in the midrash about Joseph, his bad reports about his brothers came back on him.

sources.quote: וְהַכֹּל דִּבְרֵי הֶבֶל
sources.says: Rashi says the poor man's talk of relatives and friends is all empty words.

sources.quote: לוֹ קְרִינָן וּמְרַדֵּף אֲמָרִים לַהֲנָאָתוֹ, וּלְעִנְיַן יוֹסֵף לוֹ הֵמָּה, כִּי עָלָיו חָזְרוּ דִּבָּתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says we read לו: he chases words for his own good, and for Joseph the bad reports came back on him.

19:13.headline: A dripping roof that drives you out, or never stops
19:13.body: Metzudat Zion and Ibn Ezra read טרד from the Aramaic in Daniel, 'driving out', like a quarrelsome wife who drives her husband away. Ibn Ezra also gives 'never still', a drip that does not stop.

sources.quote: טורד. ענין גרושין כמו ולך טרדין
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means driving out, as in Daniel 'they will drive you out'.

sources.quote: דלף טורד ענינו מגרש בני אדם כן מדיני אשה, כמו טרדין
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the drip drives people out, and so do a wife's quarrels.

sources.quote: פרוש אחר: דלף טורד - שלא ישקוט
sources.says: Ibn Ezra gives another reading: a drip that never rests.

19:18.headline: Do not kill him, or do not be moved by his crying
19:18.body: המיתו can come from מות, death, or from המה, to moan. Rashi reads it as not striking a deadly blow, while Ralbag reads it as not letting the child's wailing stop you from disciplining him.

sources.quote: אַל תַּכֵּהוּ מַכַּת מָוֶת
sources.says: Rashi says do not strike him a deadly blow.

sources.quote: ואף על פי שיצעק ויהמה בהכותך אותו לא תשא נפשך אל המייתו וצעקתו
sources.says: Ralbag says that even if the child cries and moans when you strike him, do not let his wailing move you to stop.

19:22.headline: A man's kindness, or his shame?
19:22.body: חסד usually means kindness, and Rashi reads it that way: people are drawn to a person for his kindness. Ralbag reads it as disgrace: what a man craves by nature is his shame.

sources.quote: עִקָּר שֶׁהַבְּרִיּוֹת מִתְאַוִּים לָאָדָם בַּעֲבוּר חַסְדּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says people desire a person mainly for his kindness.

sources.quote: הנה תאות האדם היא בטבע מה שהוא חרפה לו
sources.says: Ralbag says a person's natural craving is for what disgraces him.

19:22.headline: A man's desire, or his beauty, is his kindness
19:22.body: תאות usually means desire, and Ibn Ezra first reads it as a person always wanting to do kindness. He then offers that it may come from נאוה, 'lovely', so a person's beauty is his kindness.

sources.quote: תאות אדם - תהיה לעשות חסדו, כלומר יתאוה תמיד לעשות חסד למי שראוי לו, או תאות מן נאוה קדש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says a person should always desire to do kindness, or that תאות comes from נאוה, as in 'holiness befits Your house'.

19:27.headline: Stop straying from wise words, or get lost in them
19:27.body: שגה can mean to stray or to be carried away. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it as straying from words of knowledge, while Ralbag says you should always be carried away by love for them.

sources.quote: חֲדַל בְּנִי לִשְׁגּוֹת מֵאִמְרֵי דָעַת בִּשְׁבִיל לִשְׁמֹעַ מוּסָר
sources.says: Rashi says the verse is short and means: stop straying from words of knowledge, so that you hear instruction.

sources.quote: לשגות. מל׳ שגגה ומשגה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from error and mistake.

sources.quote: אבל ראוי שתשגה תמיד באהבת אמרי דעת
sources.says: Ralbag says you should always be absorbed in love of words of knowledge.

19:28.headline: A false witness dresses up his case, or mocks justice
19:28.body: Ibn Ezra gives both senses of יליץ: from מליץ, the witness speaks as if his word were justice, or from לץ, he mocks justice. Metzudat David says he polishes his words so people will believe him.

sources.quote: ידבר שעדותו הוא משפט וצדק מן המליץ, או ידבר ליצנות על המשפט
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he speaks as if his testimony were justice, from מליץ, or he speaks mockery against justice.

sources.quote: במשפט יתקן אמריו במיטב המליצה למען יקובלו על הלב ויאמינו לו
sources.says: Metzudat David says he dresses his words in fine speech so they will be accepted and believed.

19:28.headline: The wicked swallow their wrongdoing, or it swallows them
19:28.body: Ralbag and Metzudat David read it as the wicked swallowing their wrong, hiding it inside smooth words. Rashi turns it around: the wrong will swallow them.

sources.quote: פי רשעים יבלע ויכסה האון אשר במחשבתם
sources.says: Ralbag says the mouth of the wicked swallows and covers the wrong in their thoughts.

sources.quote: דברי האון יאמר בבליעה לבל ירגישו
sources.says: Metzudat David says he says the wicked words swallowed, so no one notices.

sources.quote: הָאָוֶן יִבְלָעֵהוּ
sources.says: Rashi says the wrongdoing will swallow him.

2:7.headline: Wisdom is called תושיה because it 'is' and lasts forever
2:7.body: Ibn Ezra and Metzudat Zion read תושיה as built on יש, 'there is': wisdom that exists and never fades. Metzudat Zion adds the sages' reading: Torah wears down the body of the one who studies it.

sources.quote: תושיה - התי״ו נוסף מן יש ותקרא כן החכמה, בעבור שהיא יש ועומדת לעד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the ת is added to יש, and wisdom is called this because it exists and stands forever.

sources.quote: התורה נקראת תושיה מלשון יש כי ישנה לעולם ולא תשוב לאין
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the Torah is called תושיה from יש, because it exists forever and does not return to nothing.

sources.quote: ורז״ל אמרו ע״ש שמתשת גוף האדם הלומדה
sources.says: He adds that the sages said it is named for weakening the body of the person who studies it.

2:15.headline: Rashi learns what נלוז means from the word beside it
2:15.body: Rashi says נלוז always means crooked, because everywhere it appears it sits next to עקש, which means bent. Here both words describe twisted paths.

sources.quote: כָּל לְשׁוֹן ׳נָלוֹז׳ לְשׁוֹן ׳עַקְמִימוּת׳ הוּא, שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם הוּא סָמוּךְ לְ׳עִקֵּשׁ׳
sources.says: Rashi says every use of נלוז means crookedness, since everywhere it is placed next to עקש.

sources.quote: ונלוזים. נוטים מדרך הישר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means turning away from the straight road.

2:16.headline: The 'strange woman': a seductress, or heresy?
2:16.body: Metzudat David reads her plainly as another man's wife, and Ralbag as the body's cravings. Rashi says she stands for heresy, because it would be odd for wisdom to guard you from adultery and from no other sin.

sources.quote: מאשה זרה היא אשת איש שהיא זרה לך
sources.says: Metzudat David says the strange woman is a married woman who is a stranger to you.

sources.quote: מִכְּנֵסִיָּה שֶׁל אֲפִיקוֹרְסוּת וְהִיא הַמִּינוּת
sources.says: Rashi says she is the assembly of unbelievers, that is, heresy.

sources.quote: כִּי מַה שִּׁבְחָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה שֶׁאָמַר כָּאן לְהַצִּילְךָ מֵאִשָּׁה זָרָה וְלֹא מֵעֲבֵירָה אַחֶרֶת
sources.says: Rashi asks what praise of Torah it would be to save you from a strange woman and not from any other sin.

sources.quote: להצילך מאשה זרה והיא הנפש המתאוה כי היא זרה ונכריה לאדם
sources.says: Ralbag says the strange woman is the craving part of the soul, which is foreign to what makes a person human.

2:18.headline: What sinks toward death: her house, or the woman herself?
2:18.body: The commentators split on who does the sinking. Rashi says her house is like a slope sliding down to death, while Ibn Ezra says the woman herself sinks to death, and death is her house.

sources.quote: כִּי תָבֹא אֶל בֵּיתָהּ, יָשַׁח וּמַחֲלִיק כְּמִדְרוֹן הַיּוֹרֵד אֶל מָוֶת
sources.says: Rashi says when you come to her house, it sinks and slides like a slope going down to death.

sources.quote: כי שחה - האשה עצמה שחה אל מות שהוא ביתה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the woman herself sinks to death, which is her house.

2:18.headline: The dead are called רפאים, the slack ones
2:18.body: Ibn Ezra says רפאים means the dead, from נרפים, gone slack, because their strength is spent. Rashi reads it as people who grow slack in doing good until they fall.

sources.quote: רפאים - מתים והוא מלשון נרפים, בעבור שתשש כחם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says רפאים are the dead, from the word for slack, because their strength has failed.

sources.quote: נִרְפִּים מִדֶּרֶךְ הַטּוֹב וְנֶעֱזָבִים מֵאֵין סוֹמֵךְ
sources.says: Rashi says they are people who go slack from the good way and are left with no one to hold them up.

sources.quote: הם המתים שנרפו ונחלשו וכוחם תש
sources.says: Metzudat David says they are the dead, who went slack and grew weak until their strength was gone.

20:1.headline: Is wine the mocker, or the man who drinks it?
20:1.body: The Aramaic Targum reads the verse plainly: wine is a mocker. Ibn Ezra, Radak and Metzudat David say a word is left unsaid: the man of wine, the drinker, is the mocker.

sources.quote: מְמִקְנָא הוּא חַמְרָא
sources.says: The Targum renders 'wine is a mocker'.

sources.quote: לץ היין - חסר איש היין לץ
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says a word is missing: 'the man of wine' is a mocker.

sources.quote: וְכֵן ״לֵץ הַיַּיִן״ (משלי כ:א) שׁוֹתֵה הַיַּיִן
sources.says: Radak says 'mocker of wine' means the one who drinks wine.

sources.quote: שותה היין הוא לץ
sources.says: Metzudat David says the wine drinker is a mocker.

20:3.headline: A rare word: the fool bursts out and shows himself
20:3.body: יתגלע is a rare word. Metzudat Zion reads it as יתגלה, "is exposed", and Rashi says the fool's shame comes out, while Ibn Ezra reads it as getting tangled up in the quarrel.

sources.quote: יתגלע. כמו יתגלה בה״א
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the same as יתגלה, 'is revealed', spelled with ה.

sources.quote: שֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׁבַת מֵרִיב, תִּגָּלֶה קְלוֹנוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says that a fool who does not stop quarreling will have his shame revealed.

sources.quote: יתגלה - יתערב במריבה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means he mixes himself into the quarrel.

20:8.headline: The judge scatters evil, or sees it all spread out
20:8.body: זרה means to scatter, as in winnowing. The Targum has the king scatter all evil from before him, while Metzudat Zion and Metzudat David read it as spread out: every wrong, even a hidden one, lies open before God's eyes.

sources.quote: מְפַזֵר מִן קָדָמוֹהִי כֻלְהוֹן בִּישְׁתָּא
sources.says: The Targum renders 'he scatters all evil from before him'.

sources.quote: מזרה. ענין פרישה ושטיחה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means spreading out, as a net is spread.

sources.quote: אז מפוזר ושטוח בעיניו כל רעות בני האדם אף אם עשאום בסתר
sources.says: Metzudat David says that when God sits in judgment, every human wrong is spread out before Him, even if done in secret.

20:14.headline: "Bad, bad," says the buyer: a haggler, or a student
20:14.body: Read plainly, a buyer runs down the goods to get a low price, then boasts of his bargain. Rashi reads the buyer as someone gaining Torah through hunger and hardship, who complains at first and is proud of it later.

sources.quote: וראה הקונה שיאמר על הממכר רע רע ויבזהו, כדי שיוכל לקנות בזול
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the buyer calls the goods bad and belittles them so he can buy cheaply.

sources.quote: הַקּוֹנֶה תּוֹרָה עַל יְדֵי הַדְּחָק וְיִסּוּרֵי רְעָבוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says it is one who gains Torah through hardship and hunger, who complains and then boasts of what he suffered.

20:21.headline: Read "rushed", written "loathed": a grabbed inheritance
20:21.body: The word is read מבהלת, rushed, but written מבחלת. Ibn Ezra says the written form hints that God loathes an inheritance taken by theft, and Rashi points to the tribes who rushed to claim land east of the Jordan and were exiled first.

sources.quote: וכתוב מבוחלת בחי"ת להודיע כי נחלה גזלה היא נמאסת ונגעלת לשם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is written with ח to show that a stolen inheritance is loathsome to God.

sources.quote: כְּגוֹן בְּנֵי גָד וּבְנֵי רְאוּבֵן שֶׁמִּהֲרוּ לִטּוֹל חֶלְקָם בְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן
sources.says: Rashi gives the tribes of Gad and Reuben, who hurried to take their share across the Jordan.

sources.quote: שֶׁגָּלוּ כַּמָּה שָׁנִים קֹדֶם שְׁאָר הַשְּׁבָטִים
sources.says: Rashi says that is why it ended without blessing: they went into exile years before the other tribes.

20:25.headline: Gulping down what is holy, or spoiling it
20:25.body: ילע is a rare word. Ibn Ezra reads it as swallowing, from related words in Job, while Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it as spoiling: a person's sins ruin his own holiness.

sources.quote: וילע מן בלעיך, יעלעו דם כמו יבלע
sources.says: Ibn Ezra links ילע to words in Job about swallowing, and says it means 'swallows'.

sources.quote: כְּשֶׁאָדָם נִכְשָׁל וְנוֹקֵשׁ בַּעֲבֵירוֹת, מְקַלְקֵל אֶת קְדֻשָּׁתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says that when a person stumbles into sins, he spoils his holiness.

sources.quote: ילע. ענין השחתה ובלבול
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means ruin and confusion.

20:26.headline: A threshing wheel, or the wheel of payback
20:26.body: Ibn Ezra reads אופן as a threshing wheel that crushes the wicked. Metzudat David and Rashi see a wheel that comes back around: what the wicked did returns to them, as with Pharaoh's army.

sources.quote: השיב עליהם אופן עגלה לדוש אותם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the king brings a cart wheel over them to thresh them.

sources.quote: כאופן המתגלגל ושב למקומו כן ישוב הגמול אל המעשה
sources.says: Metzudat David says that as a wheel rolls back to its place, so the payback returns to the deed.

sources.quote: גַּלְגַּל מִדָּתָם הֵשִׁיב עֲלֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says God turned the wheel of their own conduct back on them, as at the Sea against Pharaoh.

20:27.headline: The soul is God's lamp, or God's lamp searches the soul
20:27.body: Ibn Ezra first reads the soul as a lamp lit from God's light, searching a person's inner rooms. In a second reading God's light is the lamp, and it searches the soul, and Rashi says the soul testifies about a person in judgment.

sources.quote: כי הנשמה אצולה מאורו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the soul is drawn from God's light, which is why it is called His lamp.

sources.quote: נר אלהים חופש נשמת אדם
sources.says: In a second reading, Ibn Ezra says God's lamp searches a person's soul.

sources.quote: הַנְּשָׁמָה שֶׁבְּקִרְבּוֹ מְעִידָה עָלָיו בַּדִּין
sources.says: Rashi says the soul inside a person testifies about him in judgment.

21:4.headline: The lamp of the wicked, or their plowed field
21:4.body: נר usually means a lamp, and the Aramaic Targum translates it that way. Rashi and Ibn Ezra read it as ניר, a plowed field: what the wicked plow and plan is their sin.

sources.quote: וּשְׁרָגָא דְרַשִׁיעֵי לְחֶטְאָה
sources.says: The Targum translates 'and the lamp of the wicked is for sin'.

sources.quote: הוּא נִיר שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים – חֲרִישׁוּתָם וּמַחְשְׁבוֹתָם הוּא חַטָּאתָם
sources.says: Rashi reads it as the plowed field of the wicked: their plowing and their plans are their sin.

sources.quote: וטעמו שיניר ויחרוש הרשע
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says a letter is missing and the sense is that the wicked man breaks ground and plows.

21:5.headline: Honest, sharp, or quick: what kind of planner is חרוץ
21:5.body: Rashi here reads חרוץ as an honest man who deals truthfully. On Exodus he reads the same phrase as a sharp, keen-minded man. Metzudat Zion puts both together: quick and upright.

sources.quote: אָדָם יָשָׁר הַמִּתְהַלֵּךְ בֶּאֱמֶת וּבְמִשְׁפָּט חָרוּץ
sources.says: Rashi says it is an upright man who walks in truth and justice.

sources.quote: מַחְשְׁבוֹת חָרוּץ" (משלי כ"א) – אָדָם חָרִיף וְשָׁנוּן
