31:24.body: כנעני is the name of a people, but here it means a trader. Rashi, Ibn Ezra and Metzudat Zion all read it that way. Ibn Ezra points to Isaiah, where Tyre's traders are called its Canaanites.

sources.quote: לַכְּנַעֲנִי. תַּגָּר
sources.says: Rashi says it means a trader.

sources.quote: לכנעני - סוחר כמו כנעניה נכבדי ארץ
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means a merchant, as in 'her traders are the honored of the earth'.

sources.quote: לכנעני. תגר כמו בת איש כנעני
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a trader, as in Genesis 38.

4:3.headline: 'Before my mother' read as 'among my nation'
4:3.body: Rashi reads אמי, 'my mother', as אומתי, 'my nation': Solomon was chosen and loved among his people like a tender only son. Ralbag hears Israel speaking, the only nation that accepted the Torah.

sources.quote: רַךְ וְיָחִיד לִפְנֵי אִמִּי. לְאֻמָּתִי אֲנִי נִבְחָר וְחָבִיב כְּבֵן רַךְ וְיָחִיד
sources.says: Rashi says 'before my mother' means that in his nation he was chosen and beloved like a tender only son.

sources.quote: והייתי אז יחיד לפני אמי כי אומה אחרת לא קבלה התורה זולתי
sources.says: Ralbag says Israel was 'only' before its mother because no other nation accepted the Torah.

4:7.headline: Pay all you own for wisdom, or keep learning on your own
4:7.body: Ibn Ezra reads קנינך as money: buy wisdom with part of your wealth, and if that is not enough, give all of it. Rashi reads it as stages of learning: first take from a teacher, then work out the reasons yourself.

sources.quote: במקצת הונך ואם לא תוכל לדעתה, תן כל הונך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says to buy wisdom with part of your wealth, and if you still cannot know it, give all your wealth.

sources.quote: וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּכָל קִנְיָנְךָ קְנֵה בִינָה, תִּתְבּוֹנֵן בָּהּ מֵעַצְמְךָ לְהַשְׂכִּיל הַטְּעָמִים
sources.says: Rashi says after learning from a teacher, gain understanding by thinking it through yourself to grasp the reasons.

4:8.headline: Search wisdom over and over, or raise it high
4:8.body: Rashi reads סלסלה as going back over wisdom again and again, like a grape picker combing the vines for the last grapes. Ibn Ezra reads it as 'raise it up', from the word for building up a road.

sources.quote: חַפְּשֶׂהָ, הֱיֵה חוֹזֵר עָלֶיהָ לְדַקְדֵּק בָּהּ. כְּמוֹ ״כְּבוֹצֵר עַל סַלְסִלּוֹת״
sources.says: Rashi says it means search it and keep going over it closely, like a grape picker over the vine shoots.

sources.quote: סלסלה - הגביהה ורוממה מן סולו לרוכב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means raise it high, from 'build up a road for the rider'.

sources.quote: סלסלה. ענין משמוש כמו כבוצר על סלסלות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means handling it over and over, like a grape picker on the vines.

4:15.headline: Maimonides: the name Satan comes from this word for turning aside
4:15.body: שטה means 'turn away from it'. Maimonides says the name שטן, Satan, comes from this very word, because Satan turns people aside from the path of truth.

sources.quote: דע ש"שטן" נגזר מן "שְׂטֵה מֵעָלָיו וַעֲבֹר"
sources.says: Maimonides says the word Satan is derived from 'turn away from it and pass on'.

sources.quote: כי הוא אשר מסיר מדרכי האמת בלי ספק
sources.says: Maimonides says Satan is the one who turns people away from the ways of truth.

sources.quote: שְׂטֵה מֵעָלָיו. סוּר
sources.says: Rashi says it means turn away.

4:22.headline: 'Life' here means gaining wisdom
4:22.body: חיים plainly means being alive. Maimonides lists this verse among those where 'life' means gaining wisdom, and he notes that true beliefs are called 'life'.

sources.quote: כמו כן נפוץ השימוש במונח הזה במשמעות של קניית החכמה
sources.says: Maimonides says the word is also commonly used to mean gaining wisdom, and cites this verse.

sources.quote: בהתאם לכך קרא לדעות הנכונות
sources.says: Maimonides says that is why true beliefs are called life.

sources.quote: המוצא חכמות התורה המה לו לחיים
sources.says: Metzudat David says the wisdom of the Torah is life to the one who finds it.

4:23.headline: 'From all guarding': keep every rule, or guard your heart most
4:23.body: Rashi reads מכל משמר as 'from everything the Torah warns against', small sins and great ones. Ibn Ezra also offers 'more than anything you guard': watch your heart against bad thoughts.

sources.quote: מִכָּל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרָה תּוֹרָה הִשָּׁמֶר נְצֹר לִבְּךָ
sources.says: Rashi says to guard your heart from everything the Torah warns against.

sources.quote: יותר מכל משמר נצור לבך מלהרהר רע
sources.says: Ibn Ezra offers: more than any other guarding, guard your heart from thinking bad thoughts.

4:26.headline: Level your path, or weigh it on a scale
4:26.body: פלס can mean to make a road level or to weigh, since the beam of a scale is called פלס. Rashi reads 'weigh': set what a good deed costs against its reward.

sources.quote: שְׁקוֹל דַּרְכְּךָ: הֶפְסֵד מִצְוָה כְּנֶגֶד שְׂכָרָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says weigh your way: the loss from doing a mitzvah against its reward.

sources.quote: פלס. ענין יושר ועש״ז נקרא מטה המאזנים פלס
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means making straight, and that is why the beam of a scale is called פלס.

5:3.headline: The 'strange woman': a seductress, or heresy?
5:3.body: זרה means a strange woman. Metzudat David reads her plainly: a harlot whose words taste sweet as honey. Rashi reads her as heresy, whose talk is just as sweet. Ralbag suggests she may stand for the part of a person that craves pleasure.

sources.quote: כי אמרי הזונה המה ערבים ומתוקים כנופת צופים
sources.says: Metzudat David says the harlot's words are pleasant and sweet as honey from the comb.

sources.quote: שִׂפְתֵי זָרָה. אֲפִיקוֹרְסוּת
sources.says: Rashi says the strange woman's lips are heresy.

sources.quote: ואפשר שירמוז באשה זרה אל הנפש המתאוה
sources.says: Ralbag says the strange woman may hint at the soul's craving for pleasure.

5:5.headline: Her steps hold up the grave, or draw near to it?
5:5.body: יתמכו usually means to hold up. Metzudat David and Ralbag read it that way: her steps prop up the grave and help death win over life. Rashi reads it as nearness: her steps come close to the grave.

sources.quote: תומכים ומחזיקים את השאול שיהיה הנפתה נופל בה
sources.says: Metzudat David says her steps hold up the grave so that the one she lures falls into it.

sources.quote: כאילו סומכים ידי המות ומחזיקים אותה על החיים
sources.says: Ralbag says it is as if her steps support death's hands and strengthen it against life.

sources.quote: שְׁאוֹל צְעָדֶיהָ יִתְמֹכוּ. לְשׁוֹן קוּרְבָה
sources.says: Rashi says יתמכו here means drawing near.

5:6.headline: Weigh the path of life, or make it level?
5:6.body: פלס can mean a scale for weighing, or to level a road. Metzudat Zion reads it as making straight. Rashi reads it as weighing. A midrash he cites says God hid the reward of each command, so no one would weigh which to keep and which to drop.

sources.quote: תפלס. תישיר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means to make straight.

sources.quote: סִלְסֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַתַּן שְׂכָרָן שֶׁל מִצְווֹת וְלֹא פֵּרְשָׁן
sources.says: Rashi cites the sages: God hid the reward for the commands and did not spell it out.

sources.quote: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תְּפַלֵּס אָרְחוֹת הַתּוֹרָה, אֵי זוֹ לִיקַּח וְאֵי זוֹ לְהַנִּיחַ
sources.says: Rashi says this is so you will not weigh the Torah's paths, which to take and which to leave.

sources.quote: אַל תִּשְׁקֹל אֹרַח חַיִּים אֵצֶל אוֹתָהּ זָרָה
sources.says: Rashi's plain reading: do not weigh the path of life against that strange woman.

5:9.headline: Your years handed to a cruel one: who is he?
5:9.body: אכזרי means a cruel one. Rashi and Metzudat David say it is the prince of Gehinnom, the place of punishment. Ralbag reads it as the cruel pull of desire inside a person. The Targum simply has 'strangers'.

sources.quote: וּשְׁנוֹתֶיךָ לְאַכְזָרִי. לְשַׂר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנֹּם
sources.says: Rashi says the cruel one is the prince of Gehinnom.

sources.quote: והנותרים תמסור לאכזרי והוא שר של גיהנם
sources.says: Metzudat David says you will hand your remaining years to the cruel one, the prince of Gehinnom.

sources.quote: תתן אל זה הכח האכזרי שישחיתך באכזריות
sources.says: Ralbag says you give your years to this cruel force, which destroys you cruelly.

sources.quote: דְלָא תִתֵּן לְאַחֲרָנֵי חֵילָךְ וּשְׁנָיִךְ לְנוּכְרָאִין
sources.says: The Targum translates 'lest you give your strength to others and your years to strangers'.

5:14.headline: Almost ruined, or ruined for almost nothing?
5:14.body: כמעט can mean 'almost' or 'for a little'. Rashi first reads 'almost': I was one step from Gehinnom. A second reading in Rashi, and Metzudat David, say: for a tiny pleasure I fell into every evil, in front of everyone.

sources.quote: כְּפֶשַׂע בֵּינִי וּבֵין גֵּיהִנֹּם
sources.says: Rashi says there was only a step between me and Gehinnom.

sources.quote: בִּשְׁבִיל דָּבָר מוּעָט הָיִיתִי עַכְשָׁיו בְּכָל רָע
sources.says: Rashi gives a second reading: because of a small thing I am now in every evil.

sources.quote: בעבור הנאה קטנה כשיעור היותר מועט הייתי עתה בכל רע
sources.says: Metzudat David says for the smallest pleasure I am now in every evil.

5:15.headline: Drink from your own cistern: your wife, or the Torah?
5:15.body: A בור is a cistern that holds collected water. A באר is a well that flows. Ibn Ezra reads the verse as a call to cling to your own wife. Rashi reads it as Torah: at first you hold only what you were taught, and in the end it flows out of you.

sources.quote: בארך - נובע מים, פירוש שידבק באשתו ולא בזולתה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the well is flowing water, meaning a man should cling to his wife and no other.

sources.quote: מִבּוֹר שֶׁנָּתַן לְךָ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְחֶלְקְךָ, הִיא תּוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה
sources.says: Rashi says the cistern God gave you as your share is the Torah of Moses.

sources.quote: תְּחִלָּה כְּמַיִם מְכֻנָּסִים, וּלְבַסּוֹף נוֹבְעִין הֵם וְהוֹלְכִין
sources.says: Rashi says at first it is like collected water, and in the end it springs up and flows.

5:22.headline: Held up by his sin's ropes, as a hanged man is
5:22.body: יתמך means 'he will be held up'. Rashi says it means he will be hanged: a hanged man is held up by the rope. Metzudat David says his own sin is that rope, and it testifies against him.

sources.quote: יִתָּלֶה, שֶׁהַתָּלוּי נִתְמָךְ בַּחֶבֶל שֶׁהוּא תָּלוּי בָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi says he will be hanged, since a hanged man is held up by the rope he hangs from.

sources.quote: בהם יהיה נשען כאשר יתלוהו בהם ר״ל העון עצמו יקטרג עליו ויפרע ממנו
sources.says: Metzudat David says he will lean on those ropes when they hang him, meaning the sin itself will accuse him and punish him.

6:1.headline: Surety for a friend: a loan, or a pledge to God
6:1.body: Rashi reads it first as guaranteeing someone's loan, then as Israel's pledge at Sinai to God, who is called our Friend. Ralbag reads it as the mind standing surety to God for the body's cravings.

sources.quote: עֲרֵבוּת מָמוֹן כְּמַשְׁמָעוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means guaranteeing money, just as it sounds.

sources.quote: אַחַר שֶׁנַּעֲשֵׂיתָ עָרֵב לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁהוּא רֵעֲךָ
sources.says: Rashi's second reading: you became a guarantor to God, your Friend, when you accepted His commandments at Sinai with an oath.

sources.quote: והוא ערב בעבורה לפרוע החוב אל הש"י
sources.says: Ralbag says the mind stands surety for the craving soul, to pay its debt to God.

6:3.headline: "Untie the palm": Rashi splits the word in two
6:3.body: Rashi hears התר פס, "untie the palm", in התרפס: pay the lender and free the hand you shook. He also reads it as humbling yourself like a doorstep that people trample, the sense Metzudat Zion gives.

sources.quote: לֵךְ הִתְרַפֵּס. הַתֵּר לוֹ פַּס יָד, לְשַׁלֵּם לוֹ מָמוֹנוֹ
sources.says: Rashi reads it as 'untie his palm': pay him his money.

sources.quote: הִכָּנַע לְפָנָיו כַּאֲסְקוּפָּה הַנִּרְפֶּסֶת וְנִדְרֶסֶת
sources.says: In his second reading, Rashi says: humble yourself before Him like a doorstep that is trampled.

sources.quote: התרפס. ענין דריסה ורמיסה כמו ושארה ברגלה רפסה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means trampling, as in Daniel 'it trampled the rest with its feet'.

6:6.headline: The ant teaches honesty, not just hard work
6:6.body: The verse sends the lazy man to learn from the ant. The Talmud adds that we could learn honesty from it too, and Rashi explains: no ant takes another ant's food.

sources.quote: ואין אחת גוזלת מאכל חברתה
sources.says: Explaining the Talmud's 'we would have learned not to steal from the ant', Rashi cites this passage: no ant steals another's food.

sources.quote: כָּל אַחַת וְאַחַת אֵינָהּ גּוֹזֶלֶת מֵחֲבֶרְתָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi says each ant gathers its own food and none steals from another.

sources.quote: שהיא אוכלת חודו של זרע
sources.says: Ralbag adds that the ant bites off the tip of the seed, so the grain it stores does not sprout.

6:12.headline: בליעל: "without a yoke"
6:12.body: Metzudat Zion splits בליעל into בלי עול, "without a yoke": a person who throws off the yoke of heaven. Metzudat David builds the verse on it.

sources.quote: בליעל. בלי עול ר״ל הפורק עול שמים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says בליעל means 'without a yoke': one who throws off the yoke of heaven.

sources.quote: מי שפורק מעליו עול מקום הוא איש און
sources.says: Metzudat David says whoever throws off God's yoke is a man of wickedness.

6:13.headline: He rubs his feet, or "talks" with them
6:13.body: Rashi reads מולל as rubbing one foot against the other, a sly signal. Metzudat Zion hears מלה, a word: he speaks with his feet, as he winks with his eyes and teaches with his fingers.

sources.quote: מוֹלֵל בְּרַגְלָיו. כְּלוֹמַר: מְשַׁפְשֵׁף זֶה עַל זֶה
sources.says: Rashi says he rubs his feet one against the other.

sources.quote: מולל. הוא מלשון מלה ודבור ר״ל כאלו מדבר ברגליו דבר הלעג
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from the word for speech: it is as if he speaks mockery with his feet.

sources.quote: כֻּלָּם מִן לְשׁוֹן רְמָזִים הֵם
sources.says: Rashi says all three words are kinds of hinting, by eye, foot and finger.

6:21.headline: "Tie them on your heart" is a figure, but tefillin are not
6:21.body: Some argued that the Torah's command to bind God's words on your hand is a figure of speech, like this verse. Ibn Ezra rejects it: this book is called Proverbs, so its words are figures, but the Torah never says it speaks in parables.

sources.quote: ואין זה דרך נכונה כי בתחלת הספר כתוב משלי שלמה, והנה כל מה שהזכיר הוא דרך משל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says comparing the Torah's command to this verse is wrong, because this book opens 'the proverbs of Solomon', so all it says is figurative, while the Torah is meant as written.

sources.quote: עָנְדֵם. לְשׁוֹן קֶשֶׁר הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says the parallel word ענדם also means tying.

6:22.headline: Walking, lying down, waking: life, the grave, and resurrection
6:22.body: Ibn Ezra reads it plainly: the teaching guards you while you sleep. Rashi reads the three times of day as a whole life: walking is your lifetime, lying down is the grave, and waking is the resurrection, when the Torah will speak up for you.

sources.quote: תשמור - שאינך יכול להשמר בעת תנומתך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it guards you because you cannot guard yourself while you sleep.
Rashi says 'when you lie down' means in the grave.

sources.quote: לִתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים, לַעֲמֹד בַּדִּין
sources.says: Rashi says 'when you wake' means at the resurrection of the dead, to stand in judgment.

sources.quote: הִיא תְשִׂיחֶךָ. תָּלִיץ בַּעֲדֶךָ
sources.says: Rashi says 'it will talk with you' means it will plead for you.

6:23.headline: A commandment is a lamp, the Torah is daylight
6:23.body: Rashi says a lamp burns for a while and daylight lasts, so the merit of one commandment lasts for a time while Torah study protects always. He also reports a Talmud reading: Sabbath and Hanukkah lamps bring the light of Torah, children who become scholars.

sources.quote: כָּךְ הַתּוֹרָה עוֹמֶדֶת זְכוּתָהּ לְעוֹלָם אֶל הָאָדָם; וּזְכוּת מִצְוָה לְפִי שָׁעָה, כְּאוֹר הַנֵּר
sources.says: Rashi says the merit of Torah stays with a person always, while the merit of a commandment lasts for a time, like the light of a lamp.

sources.quote: על ידי נר מצוה דשבת וחנוכה בא אור דתורה
sources.says: Rashi says that through the Sabbath and Hanukkah lamps comes the light of Torah, meaning sons who are scholars.

6:24.headline: Who is the evil woman? Rashi says idolatry
6:24.body: Rashi argues that the Torah's whole reward cannot be just keeping you from a harlot, so the woman must stand for idolatry. Maimonides reads her as matter, which always seeks a new form.

sources.quote: וְכִי כָּל שְׂכָרָהּ וְשִׁבְחָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה שֶׁשּׁוֹמֶרֶת מִן הַזּוֹנָה לְבַדָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi asks whether the Torah's whole reward could be that it guards from a harlot alone, and concludes she stands for idolatry.

sources.quote: שדימה את החומר לאשת איש זונה
sources.says: Maimonides says Solomon compared matter to an unfaithful married woman, starting from this verse.

6:31.headline: The thief pays sevenfold, or the student gains Torah
6:31.body: Plainly, a caught thief pays many times over, and Ibn Ezra explains how the sum reaches seven. Rashi brings a midrash: the "thief" slips away to study, and "sevenfold" is the Torah, which a psalm calls refined seven times.

sources.quote: ובעבור שרוב תשלומי הגנבה הנמכרת הם חמשה וקרוב בנמצאים שנים, על כן אמר: שבעתים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the most a thief pays for a sold animal is five, and for a found one two, so the verse says seven.

sources.quote: זֶה הַמִּתְגַּנֵּב מֵאַחַר חֲבֵירוֹ הוֹלֵךְ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ וְעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi cites the Sages: the 'thief' is one who slips away from his friends to the study house to learn Torah.

sources.quote: שֶׁאֵין שִׁבְעָתַיִם אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi says 'sevenfold' means Torah, as in 'refined seven times', and that such a student ends up a judge and teacher.

6:34.headline: The husband's jealous rage, or God's
6:34.body: Ibn Ezra reads גבר as the betrayed husband, and Radak sees that rage in Potiphar keeping Joseph in prison. Rashi reads the "man" as God, mighty over all, whose anger will not spare.

sources.quote: וגבר הוא בעל האשה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the man is the woman's husband.

sources.quote: שֶׁלֹּא הִתְחָרֵט אֲדֹנָיו עָלָיו לְהוֹצִיאוֹ מִשָּׁם
sources.says: Radak says Joseph's master never relented and let him out, because he believed his wife, and cites this verse.

sources.quote: חֲמָתוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, שֶׁהוּא גִּבּוֹר עַל כֹּל
sources.says: Rashi says it is the wrath of God, who is mighty over all.

7:2.headline: The pupil of the eye, named for the little man in it
7:2.body: Metzudat Zion says the pupil is called אישון, "little man", because of the tiny image of a person you see in it. Rashi instead ties it to darkness, the black of the eye, as in אישון לילה, the black of night.

sources.quote: ובעבור קטנות צורת האיש הנראה בה קרוי אישון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the pupil is called אישון because of the small image of a man seen in it.

sources.quote: שָׁחוֹר שֶׁל עַיִן שֶׁהוּא דּוֹמֶה לַחֹשֶׁךְ, כְּמוֹ אִישׁוֹן לַיְלָה
sources.says: Rashi says it is the black of the eye, which looks like darkness, as in 'the black of night'.

7:6.headline: Looking out the window, or being seen at it
7:6.body: Ibn Ezra notes that נשקף, unlike משקיף, means to show yourself: Solomon stood at the window to be seen. Metzudat Zion says the word fits both, since whoever looks out is also seen.

sources.quote: וטעם הנשקף, להראות עצמו והמשקיף לראות אחרים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says נשקף means to show oneself, while משקיף means to look at others.

sources.quote: ולפי שהמביט לחוץ נראה גם הוא למביט בו לזה אמר נשקפתי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says that one who looks out is also seen by whoever looks at him, so the verse uses this form.

7:10.headline: Dressed like a harlot, or exposed like one
7:10.body: Metzudat Zion and Metzudat David read שית as the way she is set out: a harlot's attire. Rashi links it to a word in Samuel for the lower body, so it means a harlot's nakedness.

sources.quote: שית. ענין שימה ותקון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means placing and arranging.

sources.quote: שית זונה. ר״ל בתקון זונה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means dressed up as a harlot.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ ״שְׁתוֹתֵיהֶם״ (שמואל ב י:ד), כְּלוֹמַר: עֶרְוַת זוֹנָה
sources.says: Rashi compares a word in Samuel for the buttocks, and says it means a harlot's nakedness.

7:17.headline: Did she fan, smoke, or sprinkle her bed with perfume?
7:17.body: Rashi reads נפתי as waving, like fanning a cloth in a perfume shop, and reports Dunash's view that it means burning incense, a word with no parallel. Metzudat Zion reads it from נופת, dripping: she poured the spices on.

sources.quote: הֲנִיפוֹתִי הָרֵיחַ, כְּמֵנִיף בְּסוּדָר בְּבֵית הַבֹּשֶׂם
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'I waved the scent', like waving a cloth in a spice house.

sources.quote: וְדוּנָשׁ פֵּרֵשׁ לְשׁוֹן קִטּוּר, וְאָמַר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ דִּמְיוֹן
sources.says: Rashi reports that Dunash read it as burning incense and said the word has no parallel.

sources.quote: נפתי. ענין הזלה והתכה כמו נופת תטופנה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means pouring and melting, as in 'lips drip honey'.

7:19.headline: She says "the man", not "my husband"
7:19.body: Ibn Ezra notes she does not say "my husband", because in her betrayal he counts for nothing to her. Rashi, who reads her as heresy, hears "the man is not home" as the claim that God has left.

sources.quote: האיש - ולא אמרה אישי, כי אינו נחשב בעיניה מאומה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says she said 'the man' and not 'my husband' because he counts for nothing in her eyes.

sources.quote: רְאִיתֶם שֶׁסִּלֵּק הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שְׁכִינָתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi reads it as 'you see that God has removed His presence'.

7:20.headline: A day named for a throne, or for the hidden moon
7:20.body: כסא usually means a throne. Rashi reads the word as a fixed date, Ibn Ezra as the new moon, when the moon is covered (כסה), and Ralbag as the New Year, when God sits on His throne to judge.

sources.quote: לְיוֹם הַכֵּסֶא. לִזְמַן הַמּוֹעֵד הַקָּבוּעַ
sources.says: Rashi says it means the set time that was fixed.

sources.quote: הכסא - ראש חודש שיתכסה בו הירח
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is the new moon, when the moon is covered.

sources.quote: ואולם נקרא כן כי אז הש"י ע"ד משל יושב על כסא לשפוט תבל בצדק
sources.says: Ralbag says it is the New Year, so called because then God, so to speak, sits on a throne to judge the world.

7:21.headline: Her "teaching" is what takes him
7:21.body: לקח often means teaching, as in a good lesson. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it here as her practiced skill, while Ralbag hears לקח, to take: her words take his heart.

sources.quote: לקחה. ענין למוד והרגל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means learning and practice.

sources.quote: שֶׁהִיא לְמוּדָה לְהַרְגִּיל בְּכָךְ אֲנָשִׁים
sources.says: Rashi says she is practiced at drawing men into this.

sources.quote: דבריה הלוקחים לבו
sources.says: Ralbag says it is her words that take his heart.

7:22.headline: Snake venom or an ankle chain: two readings of עכס
7:22.body: Rashi reads עכס as a snake's venom, and in the Talmud explains the name: the snake lets it out only in anger, כעס. Ibn Ezra reads it as an ankle chain, like a shackle: a fool resists discipline as a foot resists a shackle.

sources.quote: וּכְעֶכֶס. זֶה אֶרֶס נָחָשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says עכס is a snake's venom.

sources.quote: וקרי לה עכס על שם שאינו מטילו אלא על ידי כעס
sources.says: Rashi says the venom is called עכס because the snake releases it only in anger.

sources.quote: תראנה העכסים והם דומים לכבל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says עכסים are ankle ornaments that look like a shackle, and a fool is as hard to bring to discipline as a foot into one.

8:14.headline: Sound wisdom, or the power to wear down temptation
8:14.body: Ralbag reads תושיה as grasping the true order of things. The Metzudot hear the root תשש, to weaken: Wisdom is what wears down the pull toward evil.

sources.quote: ותושיה. תשות הכח
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means weakening of strength.

sources.quote: ר״ל על ידי יותש כח היצר הרע
sources.says: Metzudat David says that through Wisdom the strength of the evil inclination is weakened.

sources.quote: ולי ג"כ תושיה רוצה לומר השגת הנימוס המושכל אשר בדברים
sources.says: Ralbag says תושיה means grasping the order that the mind finds in things.

8:15.headline: "Kings rule through me": the Sages call scholars kings
8:15.body: Rashi reads the kings here as people who rule by Wisdom's laws. Elsewhere he notes that the Sages call a Torah scholar a king, and that they learn it from this verse.

sources.quote: שֶׁהַדִּינִים וְהַמִּשְׁפָּטִים אֲנִי מְלַמְּדָם
sources.says: Rashi has Wisdom say that she teaches them the laws and judgments.

sources.quote: מלך קרי לתלמיד חכם דכתיב (משלי ח׳:ט״ו) בי מלכים ימלוכו
sources.says: Rashi says a Torah scholar is called a king, because of this verse.

sources.quote: מְלָכִים. אֵלּוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
sources.says: Rashi reads 'kings' in a psalm as Torah scholars, citing this verse.

8:17.headline: An extra letter nun hints at fifty gates of understanding
8:17.body: ימצאנני, "they will find me", has one more nun than it needs. Rashi says the nun, whose value is fifty, hints that seekers will reach the fifty gates of understanding.

sources.quote: נוּ״ן יְתֵרָה: חֲמִשִּׁים שַׁעֲרֵי בִינָה אַמְצִיאֶנּוּ
sources.says: Rashi says the extra nun means: I will let him find the fifty gates of understanding.

8:22.headline: Did God acquire Wisdom, or create her?
8:22.body: קנה usually means to acquire. Ibn Ezra and Metzudat David tie it to God as "maker of heaven and earth" in Genesis, and the Aramaic Targum translates plainly: God created me.

sources.quote: אֱלָהָא בָרְאֲנִי בְּרֵישׁ בִּרְיְתֵיהּ
sources.says: The Targum renders 'God created me at the start of His creation'.

sources.quote: ברא אותי להיות קנויה לו וכן קונה שמים
sources.says: Metzudat David says God created Wisdom to be His own, as in 'maker of heaven'.

sources.quote: קנני – מלשון: קונה שמים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word is the same as in 'maker of heaven'.

8:22.headline: The Torah is "the beginning" of Genesis 1:1
8:22.body: Wisdom calls herself the ראשית, the first, of God's way. The Sages, and Rashi after them, use this verse to read the Bible's first word, בראשית, as "for the sake of the Torah", which is called ראשית.

sources.quote: וְאֵין רֵאשִׁית אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה
sources.says: The midrash says 'beginning' means the Torah, as in this verse.

sources.quote: בִּשְׁבִיל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִקְרֵאת רֵאשִׁית דַּרְכּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the world was created for the sake of the Torah, which is called 'the first of His way'.

sources.quote: ראשית דרכו - כלומר ראשית כוונתו בבריאה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means the first thing God intended in creating.

8:22.headline: "Before" His works, but not in time
8:22.body: קדם usually means earlier in time. Ibn Ezra says Wisdom came first as a cause, not in time, because time itself is one of the things God created.

sources.quote: קדימה לעולם, קדימת חיוב לא קדימת זמן, כי הזמן מכלל הנבראים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Wisdom comes before the world as a cause, not in time, since time is among the created things.

8:24.headline: Wisdom was born, as in labor, before the deep
8:24.body: Rashi reads חוללתי as "I was created". Ibn Ezra hears a birth word in it, as in Isaiah's "Sarah who bore you", and the Aramaic Targum translates "I was born".

sources.quote: חוֹלָלְתִּי. נִבְרֵאתִי
sources.says: Rashi explains it as 'I was created'.

sources.quote: מלשון: ואל שרה תחוללכם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra links it to Isaiah's 'Sarah who bore you', meaning a start, like a birth.

sources.quote: עַד לָא נֶהֱווֹן תְּהוֹמֵי אִתְיְלִידֵית
sources.says: The Targum renders 'before the depths existed, I was born'.

8:29.headline: The sea's limit set at creation, with a split built in
8:29.body: Plainly, God set a boundary the sea may not cross. Rashi adds a midrash: when God made the Sea of Reeds He set a condition that it would split for Moses.

sources.quote: וְגָזַר עַל יַם סוּף כְּשֶׁבְּרָאוֹ, עַל מְנָת לְהִבָּקַע לִפְנֵי מֹשֶׁה
sources.says: Rashi says God decreed on the Sea of Reeds, when He created it, that it would split before Moses.

sources.quote: בעת שם לים חוק וגבול
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is when God gave the sea a law and a border.

9:1.headline: Wisdom is plural here: one Wisdom, or many wisdoms?
9:1.body: חכמות is a plural form, yet the verb בנתה, 'she built', is singular. Ibn Ezra compares other plural nouns that take a singular verb, while Metzudat David reads it as many wisdoms, each building its own house.

sources.quote: חכמות בנתה ביתה - כמו: בנות צעדה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra compares the phrase to 'daughters, she stepped', another plural noun with a singular verb.

sources.quote: חכמות. כל אחת מהחכמות בנתה בית לעצמה
sources.says: Metzudat David says each of the wisdoms built a house for itself.

sources.quote: בְּחָכְמָה בָּנָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת הָעוֹלָם
sources.says: Rashi says it means God built the world with wisdom.

9:1.headline: What are Wisdom's seven pillars?
9:1.body: The commentators ask what the seven pillars stand for. Rashi says the seven days of creation or the seven books of the Torah, Ibn Ezra says seven branches of wisdom, and Ralbag says seven just means 'many'.

sources.quote: שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית. דָּבָר אַחֵר: שִׁבְעָה סְפָרִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi says they are the seven days of creation, or the seven books of the Torah.

sources.quote: והעמודים הם שבע החכמות, שבית החכמה נכון עליהם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the pillars are the seven branches of wisdom on which its house stands.

sources.quote: כי מספר השבעה יאמר על הרבוי
sources.says: Ralbag says the number seven is used to mean many.

9:3.headline: The 'wings' of the city: its highest points
9:3.body: גפי is a rare word. Metzudat Zion links it to a later Hebrew word for wings, a place high enough for birds to fly. Ibn Ezra reads it as גבי, 'tops', since the letters ב and פ can swap.

sources.quote: גפי. ענין כנף ובדרז״ל עד בין אגפים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means wing, as in the Sages' phrase 'between the wings'.

sources.quote: כמו גבי, כי אותיות בומ"ף מתחלפות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is like גבי, 'tops', because the letters ב, ו, מ and פ can replace each other.

9:6.headline: 'Leave, simple ones' or 'leave simpleness'?
9:6.body: Ibn Ezra reads פתאים two ways. It may call out to the simple people, or it may name the thing to give up, simpleness itself, as Rashi also reads it.

sources.quote: עזבו פתאים - תאר לבעלי הפתיות וטעמו עזבו הפתאים וסורו אלי. פרוש אחר: קבוץ שם הפתיות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it names the simple people, or, in another reading, is a plural noun for simpleness.

sources.quote: עִזְבוּ פְתָאיִם וִחְיוּ. אֶת דֶּרֶךְ הַפַּתְיוּת
sources.says: Rashi says it means leave the way of simpleness.

9:7.headline: Whose blemish: the one who rebukes, or the wicked man's?
9:7.body: Rashi says the blemish falls on the person who rebukes, because the wicked man insults him back. Ibn Ezra also offers the other reading: it is the wicked man's own flaw.

sources.quote: מוּם הוּא לַמּוֹכִיחַ, שֶׁזֶּה מְחָרְפוֹ וְאֵינוֹ שׁוֹמֵעַ לוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it is a blemish for the rebuker, since the wicked man insults him and does not listen.

sources.quote: פרוש אחר: חוזר לרשע מומו - לעצמו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra offers another reading in which the blemish belongs to the wicked man himself.

9:10.headline: Knowledge of 'holy ones': of God, of angels, or of holiness
9:10.body: קדשים is plural. Ibn Ezra says some read it as God, as in 'He is a holy God', and he adds it may mean knowing the angels and spiritual beings. Metzudat David reads it as making yourself holy.

sources.quote: ודעת קדושים - פירשוהו על השם יתברך, כאמרו: כי אלהים קדושים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it has been read as God, as in 'for He is a holy God'.

sources.quote: דעת קדושים היא השגת מציאות השכלים הנפרדים והרוחניות כלם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra adds it may mean grasping that the pure minds and all spiritual beings exist.

sources.quote: ודעת קדושים. לקדש עצמו במותר לו
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means making oneself holy even in what is allowed.

9:11.headline: 'Years of life': a good living, or life to come
9:11.body: Rashi reads 'years of life' as years of income and wealth. Metzudat David reads them as added life in the world to come.

sources.quote: שָׁנִים שֶׁל חַיִּים הֵם שֶׁל פַּרְנָסָה וְעֹשֶׁר
sources.says: Rashi says years of life are years of livelihood and wealth.

sources.quote: ויתוסף לך בזה שנות חיים בעוה״ב
sources.says: Metzudat David says you will gain years of life in the world to come.

9:17.headline: Stolen water is sweet: about sin, and also about mitzvot
9:17.body: Rashi first reads the stolen water as forbidden love. He then turns it around: a good deed done in secret, when people were afraid to do it openly, also tastes sweet.

sources.quote: אַף לְעִנְיַן הַמִּצְוָה, מַיִם גְּנוּבִים יִמְתָּקוּ. שֶׁהָיוּ יְרֵאִים לַעֲשׂוֹת בְּגָלוּי וְעוֹשִׂין בְּסֵתֶר
sources.says: Rashi says that even for a mitzvah, stolen water is sweet, when people feared to do it openly and did it in secret.

9:18.headline: The dead are called 'the weak ones'
9:18.body: רפאים here means the dead. Metzudat David explains the name: the dead are those made weak and limp by death.

sources.quote: מקום הרפאים הם המתים שנרפו ונחלשו ע״י המיתה
sources.says: Metzudat David says the רפאים are the dead, who have gone slack and weak through death.

sources.quote: כי מתים שם בעמקי שאול
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reads it as the dead in the depths of the grave.
